text: I was in power on my high school track team my senior year. I had the power to push my fellow teammates and make sure that they were working hard and doing what they were supposed to be. I liked the feeling of that but sometimes I felt a little mean and didn't like having to yell at a teammate for not doing what they were supposed to be doing.

I was in the position of power when my dog wanted a treat, but did not want to do a trick for it. I had the power to not give my dog what she wanted until she did what I wanted (high-five, roll over, shake, etc.). My dog knows where the treats are located and just kept pawing at the door. I wasn't frustrated that my dog didn't do what I wanted her to, I thought it was funny. It was funny because I was in control and she was practically begging for a treat, instead of just doing a trick. Doing a trick would have been quick and easy, but instead she wanted to waste all this energy whining and pawing at the door. It feels good to have a sense of power, but I wouldn't want to be in control all the time. I wouldn't want people (or my dog in this case) to be dependent on me. My dog was dependent on me for a treat, since she can't open the door and get it herself. Eventually, I felt bad because I felt like I was teasing my dog and torturing her by not giving her her favorite snack, so I gave in and gave her a couple milk bones. She's too dang cute, with those puppy dog eyes!!

I recall a time around my junior year that I got two people together. My friend Zack wanted a girl named Taylor as his girlfriend. He wanted to be with her but he did not want to risk losing the friendship. So I decided to talk to Taylor on how she felt about the situation and she did not want to lose him as a friend either. I ended up getting them to go on a double date with me to see if anything was easier. It got a little easier as the week went on. Then I told my friend Zack he needed to ask her out already and just see how being boyfriend and girlfriend would feel. I said if you never try you will never know how you guys truly feel. In the end they dated for about 2 years and were the perfect couple. All because my friend listened to my advice on what to do.

when I was working in a nursing home and we were short staffed, other staff members came to me looking for help. I felt over whelmed at first but later on felt respected enough that they came to me for help.

One time that someone had power over me was when I ran winter track. It was during basketball season and one of the girls on the basketball team kicked us out of the locker room. We were told there was nothing that could be done since it was technically basketball season and winter track was not a school sanctioned sport. I was really angry because we still had practice to get to so we had to find somewhere else to get ready for practice. I was also annoyed because the locker room was a girl's sports locker room, not a basketball locker room. The basketball coach stood up for his players while our coach did nothing about it. Therefore, we were kicked out and had to change in the bathrooms until basketball season was over. During outdoor track season I was frustrated when the basketball team used the locker room when they were just lifting and it wasn't their season. I was frustrated because the girl that kicked us out didn't see how hypocritical she was being.
I feel good when I help any one to get what he/she want.

When I am at volleyball my coaches constantly have power over what we do. They set rules and guidelines, they are also constantly evaluating us. I hate feeling like I have no control over myself or what I am allowed or not allowed to do.

One time one of my friends came to me asking if i wanted to go to a movie with him and he really wanted to go but was only allowed if he took one other person. I was the final say and my decision would choose the outcome of either him watching this movie he wanted to see or not see it at all. I felt bad that i could not go, therefore taking away his chance of seeing it that night.

I once went to see the dentist, I lay down under the light and the dentist looked through my tooth that had serious problem. He needed to find how deep the problem went in. So he drove an equipment and went in deep to my tooth and at that time I felt that he was really taking control of my mouth and when I felt the severe pain that came from my nerve, I felt powerless and hoped it would end quicker.

I babysat for my job, and it helped give me experience for becoming a teacher. I think it was a good experience and I was able to do a good job. I have been babysitting since my freshman year in high school and over time I became more comfortable in doing my job.

One time I was put in charge of training a co worker who had just started working at my place of work. It wasn't really a memorable experience, I just showed them how to do some things and had them come back to me if they had any questions. Everything went smoothly and they seemed to catch on pretty fast.

There have been several times where I have felt to be in the position of power with my sibling. We are 7 years apart and I am the younger one. All our lives I wanted to be in control and have anything she wanted or I wanted to have more than she had. On her birthday one year, I decided to run away because no one was giving me attention, remind you I was around the age of 7. After becoming the center of attention once no one knew where I was, I felt horrible. I realized that there was no reason I should have acted that way. I cried, and I apologized to my entire family. Not only for acting out of character but because I did indeed scare everyone.

I am currently working as a manager and that position is one of power. I am the leader, the head, the boss of the other student workers. On a daily basis I have to delegate tasks to my fellow workers. The weird part about this is that they are my employees in a sense but they are also fellow students. We are on the same level, but not at the same time. Sometimes I do feel bad giving tasks out to them because I could just do them myself, but it is my job to delegate and if I do not have the time to oversee and do the task then I have to have them do it. But every task I give someone I make sure I can do myself and would be willing to do myself.

A situation in which someone else had power over me occurred when I experienced working with my new boss at work for the first time. It was fast food, I was a teenager, and it was nothing glamorous but my former boss had made the experience quite enjoyable. She'd been replaced and the new boss was not a team player, the way she had been. He liked to order people around and yell when tasks weren't done exactly as he wanted them, even though he rarely specified exactly what he wanted. I went along with my work, feeling pretty irritated, because I knew I needed the money. It's not a job I'm very fond of anymore.

This situation was over the summer when I was in a management position.  I enjoyed my time very much and I feel I help new people learn what they were suppose to know well and was able to communicate well with them.

In high school I was the captain of our girls varsity basketball team. I was voice for both the coaches and my teammates when relaying information and goals for the team. I made sure my teammates were on time to practices and games, understand deadlines and expectations, and made sure we worked together as one unit. I know at times my teammates might have been frustrated with me when I pushed them harder in practice, but I know that it was improving them and our team success as a whole. I had to be forceful, understanding, and have a good sense of leadership and listening when being in this position.

A situation where I have felt overpowered was at my High School one of my teachers was having a bad day and took it out on the students, and this case it was me.  I could not find my thumb drive that day and usually she would be very understanding and would let it be excused, however I got yelled at in front of the whole class.  It honestly made me feel awful and humiliated.  I had never forgotten anything and the one day I cannot find something my teacher made me look like an idiot.  I never forgot anything ever again after that and continue to make sure I have everything.  I understand teachers are suppose to have authority over you, but I felt like a complete idiot in front of my fellow classmates.

One time I was helping out with an event in ice skating. All the younger kids were coming up to me because I was the person who was in charge. They would come to me if they needed help or had any questions. Being in power made me feel like I was in charge and I felt important.

In high school i was in charge of organizing my schools homecoming dance. I had final say on a lot of the things going into the planning. I felt like i had to much control and it was very overwhelming at times.

The power to move up in the company in which i was working for is an incident where i did not hold that power.  Although i could help to achieve that, my manager was the one who had the decision.  If i left one thing out, he would constantly remind me that i would not achieve "Team Trainer" status.  This not only angered me, but also made me think," Does he really have the authority to hold something over me like this? Can he use this position to manipulate me?"  It bothered me, and worried me deeply.

I used to work at Applebee's. This is a corporate business so even though we have many managers, they are controlled by the corporate office. I do not agree with the way that things were supposed to be done (according to corporate) and it was very frustrating. They are very strict and have a lot of power not only over my managers, but my fellow employees and myself too.

I am a manager at a store and so one day, one of the associates was not doing what I asked of them so I pulled them aside, told them they could clock out and leave and called in another associate who would do as they were asked.

I was in a position of power during cheerleading tryouts for a club team and I was in charge of choosing girls for my own team. I felt bad for the people who weren't very good but I had to exclude them from my team. I was in their position once so I know they will be okay and if they are unhappy then hopefully they will work harder. I don't usually like having all of the power but I want things to be organized and exactly how i wanted them.

While at football, the coaches are in complete control over us, determining pretty much everything we do. They are constantly evaluating us and it is just something that i have grown used to over the years of playing sports.

Junior year of high school I was the manager of an art club event to set up the junior/senior prom. I had the ability to set people in certain positions and to do certain tasks to get our prom decorated and ready for the big night. I was entitled to critique their abilities and also set them somewhere else to do a different task if I didn't see it fit. It made me nervous being in such a position. I was very uncomfortable having to replace people once they started working and was afraid to hurt another person's feelings. It was exciting to participate and what all of it come together, but the power wasn't something I liked.
I worked at a retail store and I had to train new employees. I liked the feeling because i knew what I was doing and it felt good to help others learn something new.
Babysitting. I felt important. Yet, I felt that if I wasn't in charge something bad would happen. I had to be good at being in charge otherwise I would lose my job.

My brother wanted to move back in and my mom left it up to me to decide whether he did or not. We do not get along at all. I felt like I could finally get what I wanted with him, to not have him around anymore.
I felt in control because I decided what happened during that time period. Also, I controlled what the people around me were doing.

I am a member of the campus activities board here on campus. Our job is to find exciting events to bring here on campus through concerts and comedians, many different fun things. The last position of power I was put in was at the Mayday parade concert. The stage provided did not have a wall to block the students from climbing up on stage, so fellow cab members and myself were in charge of security. We had the position of power to stand at the foot of the stage, in front of all the fans and make sure no one touched the stage but us cab members. By doing so, we were put in a position of power and controlled the other students.

I was babysitting my cousins who were around three and five years old. I felt like I was in control and that I had the power to tell them yes or no. However, all of that power was kind of nerveracking because I had full responsibility for those kids and if something happened to them I would be in trouble and never have that power again. On the other hand, I felt like I was in control and that was a good feeling.

I had a teacher who threatened to give me an F for the semester because I skipped a band concert to go watch my sister at the NCAA Track and Field Championships. My teacher ended up giving me an A even though he told me I would fail for several weeks prior to the end of the semester. I was very agitated by his actions. If he was going to give me an A all along, then why induce a greater amount of stress? I happy to get the A, but very angry about his methods. This was not a positive experience.

my brother used to hide the house phone from me and try to lock me in different places around the house. I felt as if no one could help me because I was locked away. and when I did get out I could call my family for help. no one believed me that he would do these things.

I work for a foot doctor and when it was time for me to come to college, they had to hire someone to replace me. When they found someone to replace me, it was my job to help train them. I had the power to control what the person who replaced me was learning. It was different for me because I wasn't used to having power. I was nervous and hoped I was doing a good job at training her.

This morning, our football team had a morning lift. Our strength and conditioning coach was not in a very good mood. Players, other than myself, upset our coach and we were punished for this. Our coach made us do many forms of punishment during our lift. I did these punishments to the best of my ability and in the way that he wanted us to. I did not want to further upset him and make the group do more exercises. I was slightly frustrated about doing extra hard work for the faults of my teammates. However, I knew that we were all getting better and stronger because of the extra work.

Working as a server in an Assisted Living, I was frequently appointed to the position of training new incoming employees. This event was where I taught them how to the job, and how to do it well. Being in this position, I enjoyed telling people what to do and how to do it correctly. I feel that I do a great job as a server and I want to train people how I work because it is the best way to do it. Throughout my time working at this Assisted Living, I trained many people and I enjoyed it because I was able to see them thrive, thanks to my leadership.

While I am taking this test, if that's what you want to call it, and participating in this research study, I have someone that is evaluating me. I almost feel pressured to do well. I know the results are anonymous for this, but I still feel very pressured that I need to give the best answers possible and if I don't give good enough answers, then I will be judged.

Recently, one of my friends told me that they wanted to lose weight. Since I have extensive knowledge on the subject of nutrition and exercise, he came to me for advice on how to achieve his goal. I'm a calorie counter, so I believe that calorie counting is the overall best way to go in terms of achieving any fitness related goal. While sharing my knowledge with him and telling him the next steps he needs to take, I felt as if I had the power of knowledge that he needed in order to accomplish his goals. It felt good sharing what I know and explaining myself on the subject. He has been trying to calorie count lately, and seeing him taking my advice and trying so hard makes me feel good, and the feeling of helping someone out based on what I know is something that satisfies me.

One of the activities I was involved in at my school involved a situation in which I felt powerless. I was performing at a band competition with my color guard team and our outfits did not keep us very warm. It was late fall and very cold outside but we were not able to put on our jackets for a couple of hours and until after we performed. I was very angry and frustrated because I knew I would probably end up getting sick.

I have no car but I wanted to go to Walmart. So I got a friend to drive me there. However, I had to wait ten minutes for her. This incident made me feel helpless as I could not be as inedependent as I would want to be.

As a college athlete my coaches have control over how much time I play and can use my abilities. They use my abilities along with my teammates to win games and try to win championships. I trust my coaches to use all of our abilities in the correct ways to make us successful. I cannot put myself into the game without my coaches permission so I have no power in how much time I get to play.

When I was at my old job and I had to teach a lady with one arm how to through a discus the right way. I liked it because she was older than me and yet I was the person that was in control because I had the most knowledge on the subject. I was the teacher and the helper in that situation.

My Baseball coach had power over me in terms of whether or not I was getting red shirted. I felt extremely nervous and was scared i was going to have to red shirt. I did not get red shirted and I feel fine now.

The most powerful moment I felt was the day a friend of my mothers was at our house and he was attempting to pull her away from her marriage because he wanted to have her for himself. When I found him trying to make a move on her I was infuriated and shaking violently. However, this was during the winter and my car had gotten stuck in the driveway so I held my anger in and had him assist me in freeing it and then I let go of the barriers I was using to hold back my anger. I told him to get off of our property When he tried to play dumb about it and ask me why with a look of innocence and confusion, I informed him that I had caught him in the process of doing making a move on my mother and that he had no right to be anywhere near my mother and to do that kind of thing to her. I reminded him that he also has a wife and kids at home and that he was not welcome at our home again and if he ever did come back or tried anything with my mother again, I would be right on his doorstep to inform his wife. The whole time that I was yelling at him my mother was telling me to calm down and stop yelling but I refused and continued until he got in his car pathetically trying to apologize for his wretchedness and left. That was the most powerful experience I have ever felt keeping someone from getting what they wanted. I was livid and had made a grown man suddenly turn into a boy who had been caught doing something wrong and had cowered in regret until he could flee apologizing the whole way.

I worked as a lifeguard in a LifeTime Fitness and our supervisor couldn't handle her job and was far less experienced than I was in her position so she handed off supervising duties to me and I had to run the pool and all of the guards.  It was my job to make sure everyone was where they needed to be and deal with and complaints from the members.  I remember being exhausted from dealing with people all day but also a sense of accomplishment because I had still done a better job of coordinating everyone than my supervisor.  I thought the job would be much more difficult than it was.  Everyone listened and did what they were told to do and everything went quite smoothly after I took over.  I experienced some adrenaline whenever I had to kick people out of the pool or explain to someone what the could and could not do.  Both the members and the staff held me to a higher standard after that which made me proud.

Many of my friends frequently ask me to edit their papers for class and when I read them I can't help but judge their mistakes like improper word usage or incorrect grammar. I'll help them as much as I can without hurting anyone's feelings, and it usually goes okay once we've finished the paper. A lot of times I usually end up writing the majority of their paper for them, which makes me mad, but also makes me feel better at articulation in a weird way.

When I went home, my younger sister asked me if I would pick her and her friend up from a haunted house. I was in control because I got to choose whether or not she got to go or not. I liked having this power but I also felt bad because I wanted her to be able to have a good time.

I was captain of the cheer leading squad in high school so I was able to give directions on what to do to multiple people at one time.  They had to show respect to me and my co captain.  I enjoyed being in a higher position during high school but the responsibilities were difficult at times and it was a lot to be in charge of.  It was fun at times since people had to listen to what you had to say, but it was also a learning experience about working with others.  It taught me that not everyone is going to respect you no matter what your status is but you have to be able to handle every different type of person you come in contact with.

Teacher assigned me a paper about a certain topic. I wrote for three weeks. And i hand in to the teacher. And she evaluates the paper and gives me a score. In this process, i have no power at all. And i can't control her mind and view about my paper. I feel so nervous.

A time when someone had power over me was in high school.  I am a softball player and my high school coach made me bat left handed, even though I have never hit left handed before.  I have been very successful batting right handed but he did not even give me the chance to show him that I can actually do it.  He had the power of what I did on the offensive side of the ball for four years.  I wanted to hit right handed because that is what i knew and what I was successful at and why college coaches were looking at me to be recruited.  He took that away from me and it made me felt helpless and mad.  I hated going to practice because I was not allowed to do what I wanted.

Once I was the team leader and I had to assign jobs to each person so that things ran smoothly and effectively. I became frustrated when others didn't follow directions and work hard, but those who did what I asked of them, I was pleased with.

I work at the UPS Store and we had hired a new girl. She had some training with my manager, but one day me and her were left alone to work together. It was kind of weird because she was older than me so I automatically assume the older person has the authority, but she couldn't because she was still unsure of what she had to do so I was that person that she came to if she needed help or had any questions. I didn't mind it. I would expect her to need help and have questions because I went through the same thing. It was weird, but I'm glad she was comfortable enough to want me to help.

Recently, I was voted as the New Member Class Vice President of my sorority. The President was not there, so I was forced to instruct the other members on what to do, and what their jobs were. It was not that big of a deal, but I felt like I was helping a lot of the New Members in my sorority. It felt good that they wanted me to be in that position.

I was a treasurer in an organization and an adviser did my duties instead of me. I really wanted to step up and do everything the treasurer position had to do. I felt mad and kind of disappointed at the adviser and myself for not letting me do my job.

I was elected as a state representative when I attended Buckeye Girls State, the summer after my junior year. This position gave me the opportunity to speak as the voice for fifty other girls in my community. Public speaking terrifies me every time I have to do it; however, I felt encouraged by my peers and their positives attitudes influenced during this situation. Without their help and encouragement, I don't know if I would have been able to give those speeches in front of the crowd I had to talk to.
In this situation, I respected this person. I did not feel inferior, only more motivated.

I have always been shorter than everyone else on sports teams, this gives the other players power over me. In basketball I never got to play because I was too short to do anything. In volleyball the only position I could do well with was serving because it doesn't really involve height, so I was always over powered by the other tall players.

I babysit a 5 year old girl in the summer and if she wanted to go to the pool that day i made sure that she cleaned her room and picked up her toys first. If she didnt, then we wouldnt go to the pool. I felt bad at certain times because she didnt want to always pick up her toys but it was something that had to be done.

I was the president of National Honor Society at my high school.  I was in charge of event planning as well as informing members of upcoming events.  I also was there if anyone needed help.  Even though it could be stressful at times, I really loved it.  I got to e an authority figure but I was also able to be there for people when they needed help.  I loved helping members as well as community members through service projects we did.  I made a lot of friends and I gained experience in leading others.

I was a group leader for an assignment in class. I was in charge of assigning tasks for my group members. I enjoyed being in charge because in that situation I was the most fit person to lead. I felt like I would be able to get the job done correctly if I was heading the group. I still did my share of work, but made sure everyone else was doing theirs as well.

One tirme I had brought up a conversation with my mom about an event that was going to take place at my church. Note, my mom does not go to church. As i began to tell her that we were going to honor someone from Duck Dynasty who stood up for his beliefs on tv about Gay Marriage, she immediately took control of the situation and I could not finish what I was going to say. I felt mad because I was just telling her about an event and never said anything about me thinking one way or another, she just assumed.

I was in charge of prayer group at my highschool and held the power of dictating several choices. Often I would choose when and where to meet, what "breakfast" snack was served, when the bible study began, who took prayer requests, who prayed, and other similar decisions. I felt a sense of joy over the fact that my power helped lead to the groups success in the two years I ran it, but at the same time I felt distant from the rest of the group. I would often spend so much time trying to make things perfect that I forgot to enjoy the time I had. Most of the time though, prayer group and leading it gave me a sense of comfort and hope because it helped boost my faith as well as the faith of those who attended.

My junior year of football, I was getting evaluated to be in position to play that year. Many emotions came over me but the one that stuck out to me was being nervous because my coach that was evaluating had full power over if I got on the field that season.

I was in charge of my group project at work and what we had to. I pretty much let the group figure things out though I was only there if they really needed me to. I kept them on task and focused but when it came down to what the group was going to do i let them provide some options then i selected from those options. It was weird being in charge of a group of my peers. I didn't want to make anyone mad or have a bias on the best idea so i had them write their ideas down on paper then submit them. That way i didn't know who suggested what. When i finally chose our project i was glad because the group was not upset with my decision they went with what i thought was the best plan and they worked hard and executed it to perfection. It is weird being in a position of power or responsibility but i like it. It feels natural to me.

When i babysit i have the children do chores before we are aloud to do activities or chores. At first the children do not want to do the chores but then i keep mentioning the reward. By them doing the chores not only is the parent then happier when they arrive home but the child learns responsibility.
In high school teachers have power over you. It didn't make me feel bad because they are expected to have power over you.

Whenever I go to the store with my mom and I see something I want I ask my mom to get it for me. When she says no she tells me I can buy it with my own money, but I say no. I do not like to spend my own money on things so in those cases my mom has control over whatever I want when I shop because she only buys the things I "need." I feel angry because I convince myself and try to convince her that it is something I need.

my friend I were both running for the same position in our yearbook class, she then told me all the positive qualities I had for a different postion and made me feel like I wouldn't be good enough for this position and should run for a different one. Even though I knew I was good enough for this position it was like she was controlling me and made me feel bad about myself

I was one of the co-captains of the swim team. I tried to get the team to be one big group and cheer for the other members of the team. I was happy and honored that I had the oppurtunity because i felt that the team should be a united front and we should be one big family.

I was in a situation of power when I taught lessons in a classroom.  I felt confident and happy to be teaching students.  I thought that most of my lessons went very well and the students enjoyed themselves during the lesson. I also thought that they had a good understanding of the topics covered.
when my parents wouldn't let me go to a country concert with my friends. i was angry and upset all at once
I do not recall anytime where i was in the position of power.

I was in a job interview and I had to impress the General manager to get the job. I really needed the job. I was really nervous. My voice was shaky and my hands were sweaty. When I met the manager he scared me. He was a big man and looked mean. As the interview went on I get less and less scared. At the end of the interview he said he would call my references and give me a call after. I got a call in two days and got the job. I was so relieved.

I was babysitting my younger siblings when i was still kinda young myself. I was 13 so old enough to stay alone and i guess watch my brother and sister. I made my brother do stupid small things for me like get the remote or get me a bottle of water. My little sister was just there to watch T.V. with me. I felt great while my parents were gone but when they got back I felt really bad like I had done some thing horrible.

I was the captain of a dance team and I had to watch them and make sure they were doing routines right.  I was glad so many people relied on me.  I felt as though they all trusted me and I felt more confident in my abilities.  However, I was very stressed when I didn't know routines myself or could not help them.

My parents have power over me and when I wanted a facebook, they would not let me get one and I was very upset. I guess I felt that if I couldn't make my own decisions that I could not become an individual that had rights. I ended up getting one without their approval and when they found out they got angry. I guess when I have someone controlling me, I try to find a way around it.

By being captain of my high school dance team, I held the power to move people into forms, judge weather they should make which team, and helped decide if they were captain for the year after i graduated. Many of the dancers that I didn't think were very good were put into the back of forms or didn't make competition team. Most of these dancers thought there were the best on the team and resented me for making these decisions. Being in charge of so much made me very stressed and I hated the way my teammates resented me when I did not do something they wanted.

My senior year of high school, I was the captain of my Varsity volleyball team. I was in charge of captain meetings as well as any problems that had become evident between the girls. I felt honored to have this responsibility yet very pressured because I had never held an important position such as this ever before. I understood better what it took to hold a position in power such as team captain, and thought more of my position on the team.

When I was trying to get my friend out of her dorm, I used power of facts. I gave her a list of reasons in my head as to why it would be beneficial to go out and try new things. I could see she was nervous at first but with my persuasion and kind words I was able to control how she approached a new environment. I felt like my technical peer pressure helped her in a powerful way. By her non-verbal communication I was able to reassure her that things were going to be okay, fun, exciting and empowering. I had the power at that moment.

I'm in a position of power everyday with my children. I have a 2 year old and a 5 year old, who i am in charge of everyday. I love them very much, and thankful that i have them. i try to teach them right and wrong, moral etc.  I feel that is my duty. I love the job of a parent and feel lucky to have it.

I was helping someone train at my work one day. I felt a little more rushed and overwhelmed because I was doing more of the word and then having to explain everything to the new person. In the end of the shift I hoped that they actually picked up on a few things so the next time I worked with that person and did not have to my work and also most of theirs.

When i was the main worker at a day care center for my church, all the children there were in my charge. I had to feed them, settle their arguments and make sure they did not joke on something and die ect. Because she is such a valuable employee, I gave her permission to take the extended time off, even though it was more than she was allowed. I felt that she deserved it, and I want to keep her as a happy employee. It made me feel good that I had the power to make this exception. I felt like I was using my power for something worthwhile. It was a win-win situation.

I ran into an old short-term boyfriend at a college party. He had broken up with me about a year earlier to get back with his old girlfriend but that didn't last. Well, I had lost about 15 pounds since then and looked good and I caught him staring at me a few times. He called me up a few days later and wanted to see me. I said no way. It felt good to turn him down.
My boss has power over me while I am at work. It doesn't make me feel bad because that is his job. He does not take it too far and he makes me feel like he values my opinion.

i work as as a counselor in a "half way house," we provide services for adults with mental health/alcohol/drug problems.  a couple of weeks ago a client approached me asking for his night time medications even though it was after the time when medications are supposed to be taken.  i was in a position to either go by the rules or give him his meds.  in this situation, i had the power.  since it was only a few minutes after the "deadline," i decided to give him the medications.  my thought process was (a) i would not get in trouble for doing this, (b) the client really wanted the medications, (c) sometimes rules don't have to be enforced exactly as they are intended.

I was in charge of an important project at work. Due to the nature and time pressure of this project, several temps were brought in to work under me. They were responsible for basic administrative duties while I was working on the larger project. Because it was their job, they had to do the things I didn't want to do, or the things that would take away from my working on the actual project. I felt good that I was not being forced to take on this job and the administrative duties. It also felt good to have people assigned to make my day easier, even though they didn't like working for me. The job itself was tedious and stressful, and it helped to have assistance, even if the people assisting me weren't always as helpful as they could be.
When I was in a jam and needed to borrow some money from my dad. I felt like I had no control, and he held all the power to help me. It made me nervous, and scared.

It was when I was filing for a vacation leave from work, I was trying to get a specific day to take my leave but my boss did not grant it. Because according to him we have big volumes of work at that specific day that I am trying to request. I ended up cancelling my vacation request. I felt so bad about that since that was my daughter's birthday.

I was in charge of training 2 new employees at work. I would train the employees and evaluate their work, and then recommend one of them to because a shift leader. I felt like I was in control of the situation. The new employees worked harder to impress me, because they wanted the higher position. I felt proud and powerful.

In church, while I was practicing how to preach, our senior pastor observed us. At the end, he gave me his evaluation and advised me to do it this way and that way. I believed him because he is an experienced preacher and he delivers his sermon effectively and in an organized manner. He reminded me of exegesis and the do's and don'ts. I actually felt good when he corrected me.

One of my ex-boyfriends had a lot of power over me.  In one situation he wouldn't let me decide what I wanted to do on a date and we could only do what he wanted to do.  It didn't matter what I wanted to do.  This made me feel insufficient, embarrassed, small, and weak.

Recently, when I went in for my job interview for my current job I felt that my supervisor had power over me. She would determine if I was suitable to work for her. This made me feel very nervous, self-conscious, and cautious about how I acted. I knew she had to power to hire me or not based on her judgment and evaluation of me.

My friends wanted to go to a certain type of store to buy something but they didn't really know anything about that type of store, but I knew so I was in control on what store they should go based on my recommendations.

My World History teacher had the power over me because she determined my grade at the end of the course. I wanted an A+ and she controlled my ability to get it. I had to be the student that she was looking for and produce work that she was particularly interested in to achieve a good score. I felt powerless and ashamed that I had to pretend to be someone else in order to get what I wanted. I never want to be in such a situation ever again.

I was a coach on a little girls' volleyball team. One of my best friend's little sisters was on the team I coached and I wanted to start her and let her play a lot because I liked her, but she wasn't very good. I felt bad for not playing her most of the game but I also wanted the team to do well. I made the right choice. At least, I think I did.

It was Halloween and there was a crazy party going on. I asked my parents if i were allowed to go and they would not let me. I felt angry that they would not let me go because I knew I was going to be getting home safe. Still, they did not let me go.

Several months ago, I was given the responsibility of prepping four young girls for a school recital. I had to decide whether they were ready or not and had to make sure that they knew their parts and what they had to do. I felt like the outcome of everything was on my shoulders and whether the girls did well or not reflected my ability to lead them. It was also my responsibility to get these girls to and from the school in a timely manner. Although there was some pressure because I was responsible for more than one person, I am glad I was given the task because I learned a lot about myself my reliability, and my leadership skills.

I was a supervisor of a work center when I was in the Navy. I had to delegate duties to my subordinates, some will diligently follow my orders while others were hesitant sometimes. I remember feeling glad and happy about this opportunity and responsibilities that go along with it. I wanted to make the work center a better place, from the production side and from the emotional side, meaning I wanted everyone to be happy they work there. At times, higher ups with come down on me and I would get annoyed because of the futile reason they needed to talk to me to get stuff done, everything was going to get done if they told me or not. It just seemed pointless and a waste of time to be causing unnecessary stress to me and my work center. There was times when there were minor altercations but everything would simmer down quickly and wouldn't escalate to a worse situation. Maybe I should've been harder on myself and my subordinates.

it was approximately sixteen years ago my brother not allowing me go out with my friends. my friends came over they all were waiting on me, my brother told them I will not be going out. I felt really horrible and insulted. there was nothing I could have done my brother was much older than I am, my parents were not around he was the one in charge. I having the right to made my own decision at that particular moment made feel so bad. 'I cant wait to grow up', that's what I told myself. Being an adult now its fun and really feels good to make your own decision at times.

In my Political Science class my teacher had the power whether he would raise my grade from a B+ to an A-. Although, I had studied as much as I could and tried my absolute best on all assignments, I felt helpless when I was not in control of the grade.

In a volleyball match I had to sit and watch my team play very badly and was helpless in their losing battles. My coach who decided who played and at what times would not make any substitutions to the starting lune-up and so me amongst the other six girls on the bench with me were feeling detached from the situation entirely as there was nothing we could do to help. We had no power over how the girls on the court played and we had no power over whether or not any of us would get the opportunity to go in the game and make a change.

When applying to medical school, I recently have been going on a lot of different interviews and meeting with different faculty members and students in different places. Upon meeting these people, it is obvious that they play a very important role in the process. Most schools invite students based on academics and the interview is the last "step" needed to get accepted. I recall one particular interview in New Jersey, which was for my #1 choice school. I realized that the best that I could do is try to relax, but I felt that such a huge part of my life was in someone else's hands. It was frustrating that I worked so hard to do my part in academics, but I could lose all of that just in case my interviewer didn't like me for some particular reason that could be out of my control. I felt helpless because I could not actively do anything do get into medical school besides try my best, but there was no definite way to have a positive interaction with this person.

I was assigned as a "facilitator" in a high school Literature group project. The majority of our group (consisted of four) strongly felt that the use of a certain motif was prevalent in the book we were analyzing. However, our group leader thought otherwise. Being the group leader, not only did he or she have the power to overrule our decisions, but also turned in an evaluation form of the group's compliance and work ethic. I was livid at the fact that our leader would use his or her position for personal benefit, rather than thinking of the group as whole. I felt as though our low grade was a result of the poor decisions of our leader and if I had got what I wanted, the group would have consequently received a higher grade.

I was a county captain for my golf team, which meant that I arranged meetings to hear peoples' voices and I was able to change things if there were any problems causing upset within my team and the county. I was happy that I had been chosen to be captain as it was a big role and quite difficult to make everyone happy. I probably wouldn't like to do it again as I am not the most confident person and I do not like to be put in to bad situations that are stressful. I did enjoy the time of being in power although sometimes I wasn't very good at it.

As a lifeguard, I was able to direct people in their actions and behaviors to maintain safety for all those in the waterpark at the time. At the time I was at a position in the kid play area called "ship" where I was to look after a rather large ship with slides and tunnels. I would normally get rather annoyed with the kids that chose not to listen to warnings or commands about their actions and blatant disrespect especially towards someone in a position of authority at the time.

When I was applying to colleges, it terrified me that my career, my entire life, was in the hands of someone else. Nova was my top choice in schools, and to think that someone who had never even met me could decide my fate was terrifying. I felt slightly in control because I chose what I wrote in my application and what was on my resume, but still, all someone had to say was "no" and the path I wanted to be on would have to have changed.
I have never really been in a situation where I have had that type of power.

One of the last times that I was in a situation of power was right before I came down to Nova Southeastern University. I was working at Foodworks Restaurant, and because I have worked there for three years I had seniority over many of the younger kids. While I trained them on the responsibilities of being a dishwasher I remembered what it was like when I was being trained, only now I was in charge. If I did not want to do something I could have just told Evan or Dylan to do something and they would've done it with no questions asked. It felt good to be in control, but I did not abuse my power. I still did all of my responsibilities and didn't throw the burden onto my subordinates

At the beginning of my senior year in high school, I was asked by my dance teacher to help judge the annual auditions for the team. I was on the panel with 2 other former students and 1 current student, not including the teacher. About 50 students auditioned for the roughly 20 spots available. I gave my opinion as to who should move on each round. I assessed each individual by their level of energy, their strength in technique, and their improvement overall. Some degree of favoritism was evident for certain dancers for their immense talent shown throughout the year. For others, I had to think long and hard to determine whether they could keep up with the demands of the class. Some individuals did not have strong technique, but showed massive improvement and were well on their way to mastering technique if given the chance. I knew that for some of the individuals, it was really important to make this team. Cuts needed to be made as hard as it is seeing their disappointed faces. I was once in that spot where making the team was very important to me. For those who were in the middle, I had to envision them on the team and determine whether they could keep up or bring the team down.

One time I was in a relationship with a boy and I felt as if he somehow had power over my happiness. He would tend to be rude and at times make me feel very negative. It was a time where I felt my esteem to be very low. However, I left him and now my esteem has gone back up

When I turned 17, I had saved enough money to buy a car. My parents would not give me access to my bank account, because they didn't want me to buy a car. I felt angry and helpless. It was my money that I worked for, and I couldn't even use it. I thought that having a car would make it easier on my family and on myself. I knew that it was a huge responsibility, and I felt ready for that. After my parents explained to me their reasoning, I wasn't as angry as I initially felt. They explained that I would be moving off island in a year to go to college, so if I bought a car, I wouldn't get much usage out of it.

I was an assistant cheerleading coach for a popwarner team that I once cheered on. I made up and entire routine and taught it to the girls and two weeks before the competition the head coach decided she did not like that her daughter was in the back for a lot of the parts. I had to rework the entire routine, changing each formation to make the head coach happy because she had more power than me. It really frustrated me because I was trying to set up the routine so the team had a shot at winning and all she cared about was making her daughter show-cased.

On the basketball court, the point guard is 99% of the time in power. They call out the plays and tells everyone where to go because they have a full view of the court and can tell what the defense is giving. When I play this position, I feel as if I run the court. It is always a good feeling because you know what play will work best for what the defense is giving. If that play does not work, we simply try another play until we make a shot. But it usually works on the first try and because of that, I feel happy because my team scored.
My parents chose what high school I went to. At the time I was very upset and angry because I couldn't override their decision.

A few years ago, I babysat two little boys regularly, and they had to listen to what I had to say or had to ask permission before they did something. It was interesting because of the level of responsibility for other people, and the trust that the parents had in me. I had to be authoritative so that the kids would listen to me, but nice enough to where they enjoyed the experience and wanted me back. It didn't always go smoothly because they were both pretty stubborn, but in the end they usually ended up giving in and listening to me.
I feel as though I am in a position of power when I babysit children because I am the primary care taker of the child(ren), therefore if they want something I would have to comply first.

Several years ago, after going through a series of financially "rough" months and being involved in a serious car accident in which his right leg was severed off, my father was not allowed to leave the house (doctor's orders) and was thus in a depressed state; I had to stay home and care for him and felt powerless due to my inability to leave or engage in any outside activities.

I was vice president of a Med club in my high school. So I had somewhat of power of people in the club. The fact that I knew I could take away some people's positions if they weren't doing the job done made me be more responsible in my own position. Having that much power over a large group of people makes you be  more concise with the things you have to do. And it makes you work harder.
When I tutored a group of people on a certain subject I was in that position of power.

I served as the president of Business Professionals of America, an organization that revolves around promoting business strategies and an amalgamation of other areas such as mathematics, science, and technology, during senior year of high school. I had to work with several individuals on a weekly basis to raise funds for the group, promote ideas as to how to better the work that they have to submit for their specific events, and follow through with volunteering projects. Sometimes, the rest of the board members did not cooperate well; therefore, some tasks burdened upon me. Nonetheless, I had to balance the work by carrying out tasks independently and utilizing teamwork characteristics. Mostly, I was content, but sometimes I would have to store the infuriation inside- venting would not have been the best choice when I have much else going on already not related to the club.

Leading a team for a game in airsoft. I felt important, responsible, and looked up to. I had to create plans and lead everyone. I felt as though if something went wrong it was automatically my fault. I was looked up to, and expected to win.

A particular incident in which I was in a position of power was when I taught a dance class. I was the teacher for the class and was in charge and stretching them and teaching them a dance I made up. I always dread thinking about teaching classes because since I'm pretty close to age with most of the kids, I feel that they will end up not listening to me. As I teach the class and give instruction on what to do, I find myself actually having fun. By the end of the class, I am relieved that I was able to stay in control and keep everyone under my rule.

A past experience where I was in a position of power was when I was working at my summer job as a lifeguard. As a lifeguard it was my responsibility to ensure the safety of the patrons. If a patron was not following the rules it was my job to correct them. I had the power and authority to address the patrons and what they were doing wrong, as well as take further actions if need be. It was a good feeling to be in a position of power, even if very little.

I wouldn't like the feeling of having no power, and someone else having full power over me. I am a very independent person and I like to be a leader and lead, not a follower and listening to ones commands.

a few years ago when my parents were getting me my first car, even though I was paying for a little less than half of it I was not in what or had say of which one I preferred. My parents took over and choose the car I was getting. In this situation I felt unimportant and as if I have no say in life situations involving me.

An ongoing situation is regarding buying a car down in Florida because my mom has the control of what car I will get and when I will get it. She is willing to pay but I need to agree with her, and until she agrees that it is time, I am under her control of when I will receive a car.

My brother wanted to eat my sandwich I left in the fridge, but I told him if he did I would tell my mom and dad about his bad grades and all the bad things he did. I was happy I got the sandwich and my brother gave up fighting with me.

I was at a tryout for an orchestra camp. In front of all of the other camp attendees and the "judges" I had to perform a piece and get placed in a "seat" according to how well I did. Even though the position I would be placed in had no real consequence and didn't speak of my full abilities I was still incredibly nervous. I wasn't nervous about playing the piece, because I had practiced it so often, but because I was afraid of others judging me. I ended up being so focused on what the others thought about my playing or my looks that I messed up on part of my piece and was placed in a lower ranking than I had hoped.

I want a car on campus, even thought I'm a resident it would feel nice to leave campus without being at the mercy of someone driving you. I keep asking my parents if they could help me but they keep saying no. It's frustrating because I feel more independent when I'm driving my own car. I feel like I'm a stupid high school kid asking people for rides. I loved having my own car and driving everywhere myself. But now I can't and I'm pretty annoyed. Why couldn't I just commute? I really only live 20 min away from campus but I wanted to be away from home! If I was commuting I'd have my own car.

I was in an event like this when I was grading tests for a teacher as a teacher's aide. I liked being able to correct grammar, spelling, math, etc. and being able to let that student know it was wrong so they could correct the issue. I liked this because it helped out the student in the long run perform better on their next test.

One time in which I was in a position of power, I was leading my group in a Latin video project. I was given responsibility to direct, shoot, and edit the movie. I think that I was trusted to be able to handle these responsibilities because I had the most experience with movie equipment amongst the rest of my team. It felt especially good that I helped get my team an "A".

I was in charge of a fundraiser in which I was working with high school students. There were about 40 of them I was in charge of and they were split into different groups to do different jobs. For example: serving, ticket taking, kitchen help, etc. Since it was an important event for the high school students I had to really explain things clearly, and monitor them closely. It was also a bit stressful since I was the one in charge of each group to try, and make sure everything was going to plan before, during, and after the event. At the end, I asked for feedback on my performance as well as theirs in order to see what they thought I could have done better or they themselves could have done better. Most seemed to think I had handled the position very well, and because I was comfortable with my job they also felt comfortable in theirs.

The last time I was in a position of power was when I was helping my mom backstage for her dance recital. I was the manager and I had to make sure everyone was doing their job. I had to perform as well as take care of the girls and be sure that the helpers were doing their job. I also had to make sure the girls were in their places and being respectful of the other performers. It was very overwhelming, because I felt that I was doing a billion things at one time. I had to change various times and then take care of the younger girls as well as the helpers, because most of the time they weren't doing their job and letting the girls round around from place to place. So in that instance, I had to take over their job and tell the girls to go to their spots and be respectful. To not be so noisy back stage. It didn't feel like a recital, it felt more like a marathon with all the changes of costume I had plus taking care of everyone in those 2 hours.

When I was in the Marine Corps I was in charge of 6 Marines. I had to ensure that they performed all of their duties as Marines or I would restrict them from going home until the task were finished. Also if certain task weren't finished in their living quarters they would be restricted to their rooms until they fixed any issues.

when I was asked to help a swimteam hire a newcoach me and others decided on the canidates and evaluated experience knowledge and communication skills and presented the top canidates to a board to select final coach

When I worked in a paper with a partner and she didn't let me see what she was writing to correct any errors or add another point. I felt excluded of the work and frustrated because I wanted to have more control over it. Then I talked with the professor and he explained to the class that the paper was a team work and we should let our partner cooperate. From that moment I could also work in our paper. I solved my problem by expressing my concern.

I had taken a class where my grade was just below an A. The last assignment of the semester was a term paper, and so I spent more time than I usually would have in order to get a good grade and earn an A in the class. It is a little stressful knowing someone else had control over my grade and so I went above and beyond just so I would not be as worried about earning the grade I felt I deserved.

A time in which I were in a position of power was when I worked in the dental office, I had controlled how much individuals had to pay for their visit. I felt like I had power, like I had experience and like people looked up to me.
I held a clothing drive for poor immigrant children before Christmas. We collected nearly $2000 in clothing.

A situation in which someone had power over me was when I had to go in for a job interview to get myself evaluated of whether I was fit for the job or not. I was asked several questions regarding myself and my abilities, and I felt extremely nervous and very much under a lot of pressure to prove myself as capable for the job.

I'm no longer able to be around nor speak with one of my closest friends anymore. She is such an amazing person even though she has her flaws. She did try to brainwash me once in a while and that's why my loved ones told me she was no good for me to be with. At the end of the day she is a great person. I hate it, I feel horrible about it. She was always there for me and now that she needs me the most I cant be there for her. At the end of the day it benefit me somehow hopefully.

I had a firm desire to share and impart any of my life experiences and knowledge to the person over whom I had power.  In no way did I, and nor did I feel that I had to, try to abuse and amplify my authority over that person - I was strictly there for helping that person.  I find this methodology to be the most productive, as opposed to using power or authority as a way of committing harm toward someone in some way.

I was volunteering by working as a junior camp counselor. Specifically, I worked with the 3-4 year olds. When it was time for their snack, the children would receive a juice with two cookies (unless they brought their own snacks). Certain children would want more than two cookies, however, I made sure that they only had two cookies. My thoughts were that the children who wanted extra cookies should not have extra cookies, because #1, that was the rule, and #2, the children should not be ingesting so much sugar in such a short time (this would cause them to become extra hyper). Although I did not like to see them momentarily unhappy, I knew that is was better for their health if they did not have any extra cookies.

I was the director, musical director and the designer for the musical at Palm Beach State College called 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee. It was the first musical the school had done in almost 20 years and the first student run musical ever so the pressure was on. I had a lot of hurdles to jump when it came to cast and budget things but overall it was a very rewarding experience. I was able to express my creativity on many different levels and the show was a success. It has since opened up many opportunities for my future.

I was in a relationship in which my boyfriend was very controlling. Whenever we would be together, he would try to control everything I did. He would try to control what food I ordered, what I wore, who I talked to, etc. This situation made me very upset and I suppressed a lot of anger. I was not happy. For a long time I suffered from depression and it took a lot of strength to get out of that state. I was negative about life. However, I would never admit the fact that it was because of him. I kept excusing him for his actions. After I left the relationship and realized what had happened to me, I promised myself I would never let anyone control me in that way again and that I would live as freely as possible.

I felt like somebody had power over me when I was in 8th grade. The teachers always told you what to do and what not to do. I wasn't doing anything bad but they wanted everything done their way or it was wrong. I dint like this and it made me feel like I was powerless and a child.

A week before my 17TH birthday, my then boyfriend of three years and I got into a huge argument. I found out that he was cheating on me for a period of 10-11 months with a young lady that I did not like at all, and he knew that. I was so hurt that I deleted his number, all of our pictures, and told him that I didn't want to see him or hear from him again. He knew how hurt I was and he tried his best to make things right. On the day of my birthday, he popped up at my house after class with 5 dozen roses, 3 perfume sets, and the keys to a 2013 Porsche Cayenne that he rented for me. I refused to accept either gift. He got on his knees, begged for my forgiveness and told me that he would do anything I wanted if I accept his apology. It was at that moment, I knew that I had power over him. I told him to take me AND my immediate family members to dinner that night and he paid almost $400 at The Cheesecake Factory for almost 30 people.

I worked for a hotel and I was in charge of supervising 3 bellmen.  Some where young and some had attitudes.  I found it sometimes draining having to tell or ask them to do things.  It was the worst part of my job, at that time.

Working at my parents medical office, I was in charge of making sure that everyone was taken care of and I had to make sure that the patients left the office satisfied. One time a patient wanted something that was not necessary and I didn't allow them to get what they wanted form the doctor and they were furious, but I think that I did a good thing because I helped save their lives, eventually.
I never experienced a situation I had no power or someone else could evaluate me. I've always had control over my situations and my actions.

A position of power I was in was back in high school as part of the student government. It was during homecoming week where I felt the most power as I was assigned to be in charge of the back drop we had to do for a skit that was part of the homecoming events. I was able to dictate to a person whether or not they could do something they wanted for the back drop or not because they had to come to me and ask before they could do it. I honestly felt powerful as I could dictate if they could do it or not. Every time someone would ask me if they could paint this or that, my first thought would be, I could say no right now and they could do nothing about it. Obviously it was not the case as I wanted everyone's ideas to come together, but just the fact that I had the power to do things my way was a great feeling.

An incident in which I was in a position of power would be when I was in charge of a committee at my school's blood drive. I was in charge of the food committee, so I essentially had power to control how much food the blood donors could have, as well as the staff of my committee. At first I was very worried and stressed out because there have been numerous incidents where the food committee fails to have enough food to supply over 300 people, and this task is  particularly hard because all the food has to be donated; we don't have a budget for food. At first I was so stressed out I went to as many food places as possible to get as much food as I could, and in addition to the food the Blood Drive Staff buy for the donors as well, it was enough to last for about 2 weeks after the blood drive! I felt accomplished!

As vice president of student council I controlled the ability of my student council body to get the theme we wanted to have for our prom. As a student council body we attempted and succeeded in persuading our principal to allow for our theme to be a "Great Gatsby" theme. We were very angry when our principal wouldn't consider the idea but we continued to try for it and ultimately ended up succeeding.

positions of power I have been in is when I babysit children and evaluate or control their behavior and punish or reward accordingly. I enjoy babysitting for the taking care of them part not the controlling part though.

When my parents separated several years ago they fought over who would have custody of my sisters and me. The judge had power over me because it was ultimately his decision on who I lived with and he didn't care about what I wanted. He decided on splitting time with my parents 50/50 when all I wanted was to live with my mom. It made me very angry because it is my life and nobody should decide who I should live with but me, especially a man I had never met and knew who nothing about me. Another decision he had made was for me to go to group therapy with my dad and younger sister. Eventually I put my foot down and refused to go to therapy and see my dad. It did get me into some trouble but I feel better now that I'm 18 because he can't make me go anywhere I don't want to be.
I once manipulated my friend to go to the Cheesecake Factory with me.

A situation in which I did not have power was a recent dance tryout, in which I was the only one trying out that particular day. I felt slightly overwhelmed and very scrutinized. At times, I would feel extra uncomfortable compared to how I would feel if I was in a group tryout setting.

Planning things with friends does get complicated, for the most part we always agree on what we will do but at times we don't agree. Thinking of going out to one of our favorite places in Fort Lauderdale, but when we go it is on a school night and we always return back to campus around 2:30 am.
