One time when I was babysitting my niece and nephew they were being very destructive and loud. One of them was crying and the other was running around like a chicken with his head cut off. I told them that if they were to be good, meaning that they would calm down and sit quietly and be respectful, they would earn a prize such as candy, or extra tv time. They really wanted to have candy so I could tell that they were going to try their hardest to listen to me. I told them that if they were to be bad even once more, that they would not get either prize and would be sent to bed. You could tell that they were determined to be good, despite the prior events. In the end, they chose to settle down and be nice to one another. They earned their reward and were extremely happy.

All of high school, the administration had power over me. At times, I felt that  this lesser feeling was necessary but other times I felt powerless and not in control. I believe that the administration needs to assert their control over students, however I feel that high school students should still have a considerable amount of freedom.

At work, I can decide when I am ready to give out samples to customers. I felt in control of my boundaries when I am in this position. Sometimes customers want samples before they are ready and they wait around my sample station like vultures and it makes me feel pressured. Usually when I feel pressured, I remember that I am in charge and I am going to take my take to cook quality samples. The customers can wait an extra few minutes. I feel pissed off at customers who are impatient so sometimes I take extra long to put out samples.

One situation happened was within my boy scout troop. The leader of the troop decided that he would control everyone and get them to do things he wanted done. I voiced my opinion on his actions to him and he disregarded my opinion and continued to that way. If I had tried to do anything, he would get everyone to do it his way because he is the leader.

Last friday, I had a biology 205 test. I felt like I was really prepared for it, but in the end, my professor had the power to decide which grade I wanted. She was going to evaluate my knowledge of what I knew regarding tissues of the body as well as things about the various organelles of cells. I will find out how I did this upcoming friday, however after my test I felt very scared. Instead of being able to verbally explain my answers to her, I had to write them down. When writing, it was easier for me to go off on some sort of tangent. At this moment I am still nervous/scared to see how I did on this test, because my written answers are under her power to be evaluated. I did not know how much information she wanted from me, so I could have given her too much--or worse?Õ_ë_too little.

I was in a position of power when my boyfriend owed me money.  I kept reminding him of it when he was spending money other ways or complaining about paying for dinner.  I wanted to be right, but I wanted to be nice.  It was hard not to say something that would make him totally powerless.  I wanted him to feel guilty.

During a Cheer Competition the team doesn't have power over how the judges view our stunts or anything so we don't know how well they will score us in difficulty or variety, etc. Because judges vary and so do their opinions. It was nerve wracking each time because we would feel like we did better than the other teams but than get placed lower than them. Or other times we would get deducted for things we didn't feel like we should get deducted on. so it could be frustrating and scary at the same time.

I felt that I was in power when I was the captain of my high school cheer squad. I was a leader of the team and also had the power to control the team and judge individuals based on their ability. I was in charge of calling what we did at games, and organizing team meetings/bonding activities. I felt that this position was fun but stressful. Being one person, having to organize 20 others becomes a challenge. This taught me different forms of leadership because yelling at the girls doesn't make any progress for the team. I had to learn that being a positive influence was the strongest form of leadership.

One particular event that comes to mind is the time when I was in charge of setting up a project for my group (my group being three nine year olds). Since I was their leader, I had the power to tell them what tasks to perform to get the project completed. Honestly, I felt pretty good, there were some moments of irritation when things weren't done correctly but otherwise it felt good to know that things were getting done. I guess I'm the kind of person that likes to know exactly what happens and how the project is progressing. So me being in charge allowed me to have that knowledge first hand. Also, when the project was completed and they presented it to the rest of the class, I felt relieved that everything had gone smoothly and that it was completed. I was proud of them and happy with the work that they did.

The day I got my license I was scared. My test observer was quiet the whole time and only told me where to go. I felt uncomfortable with all the awkward silence and wished I was getting some feedback. I never knew if I was doing something right or wrong and doubted myself. Each instruction he gave me made me more nervous. At the end of the test I parked horribly and waited for my results. I was surprised to hear that I passed my test and did well since I had no feedback the whole time.

In the situation I was forced to go to a "special" meeting everyday during the school week in elementary school for extra help. We did a variety of task that I had know control over and did not like. I thought the task we did had no purpose. I also hated being pulled out of class everyday and it made me feel like there was something wrong with me. Overall I hated going to these meetings.
I work as camp counselor, so I have authority over kids. If they want to do something unsafe, I can tell them not to do that dangerous thing, and they have to listen or there will be consequences.

I held an officer position in the Key Club of my high school during my senior year. I was in charge of notifying the club of future volunteer opportunities and events (e.g. charities, food drives, etc.), making sure members were responsible and turned in their volunteer logs on time, and warned them that their membership could be put on probation if they continued to sign up for volunteer events and not show up when the day comes. Though I was an officer, I never felt like I was "in power"; I just found myself as someone who was being a bit extra helpful for my fellow club members to maintain their activeness in our community as well as the club. It was a very enjoyable experience.

As a youth group assistant at my old church I was in a position of power. I was able to determine the schedule of events during an outing. I had power over music choices and game choices. I generally felt that I was prepared but open to opinion from what the kids really wanted. I didn't like to tell kids to stop doing something wrong. I wanted to be the cool guy that let people get away with things that were probably against the rules. I didn't dwell on the fact that I had power.

When I was younger, I had a candy bar that I didn't want, that both my brothers wanted. Eventually I threw it between the two of them and made them fight for it. I guess at that age, that made me feel good to do , because I felt like I had a position of power. It was fun to watch them fight over the candy bad that I had not wanted.

When I was in a position of power was when I had to look after and take care of my little sister and three cousins while the rest of my family was at a casino for a birthday party.  I was very tired from trying to keep all four of the occupied and I was a little annoyed by how late I had to watch them and was stuck in a hotel room with them with nothing really to do.

During class registration the head of the department determines which classes you are able to take. They have power over the students in this way. It is frustrating to get classes that are uninteresting and do not apply to the career intended by the degree.

It was very nerve racking because I wanted to say something and stand up for myself, but I was also to afraid of the implications of me speaking up. The situation held a lot of tension between me and the other person of power.
the ability to lift heavy objects at a hardware store and the men decided to lift all the heavy objects when I was capable of doing it myself. I had to no choice but to let them do their job

When I was a young child I had a babysitter. She was able to influence everything I did and if I did not comply, then I was forced to be punished, via time out or things that mattered to me were taken away. I felt powerless and upset if any of these things happened- so I complied with her rules.

I have been trying to get a singe room due to a health condition and need for privacy. The disability center at PLU has completely ignored my doctors letter of recommendation and they have control whether I get the room or not. It made me feel helpless.

I think babysitting young children puts you in a position of power during the time you watch them. I've babysat young children before and I try not to put myself too high above them so as not to make them resent me. I know I've had to tell kids to behave and stop arguing, and to threaten to take away whatever it is they're fighting over or something they'd like to play with. I don't like yelling or having to take things away from kids but when they don't get along or aren't following set directions that I've been given and they won't listen to me, it's occasionally necessary. For the most part I try to lead activities we can all do for fun or let them do their own thing instead of trying to impose certain activities on them. I like being able to watch the children without having to control what they're doing. I don't want TOO much power over them or to be really depended on.

One situation I have experienced in which someone had power over me would be when I was interviewing for scholarships, particularly a scholarship for my college, PLU, before coming to PLU. I felt that the interviewer had power over me because it was up to them to make the decision on whether or not I would receive the scholarship; in other words, they had the power to either give or keep the thing that I desired from me. This made me feel extremely nervous prior to the interview, but when the I felt the interview was going well, I felt, while not necessarily confident, much more at ease because although the person had power over me, I realized that I could heavily influence that person in power. I felt that the action/decision that they were going to make was going to be a reflection of my actions - which made me feel very conscientious, but happy knowing that this seemed to be a fair situation in that sense.

I was the president for a club at my school , called Student 2 Student. We helped welcome military children and valued their transition into our school. I had to run meetings and direct the activities that we would do. At first, I was nervous to be the "leader" that everyone looked at, especially having to run a meeting for the first time. But after a while, that feeling of responsibility became comfortable and accepting. In addition, I realized that the work I was doing for this club was important and caused change within my school. So after a while, I felt empowered to always wake up and be the position as president, because I found meaning behind my work.

One time I was in a situation of power was when I was the patrol leader for my girl scout troop. While the job didn't actually involve much power, everyone in my troop desperately wanted the job when it was time to switch roles. It was highly sought after partly because you got to wear a special gold rope on your uniform. I think this was around fifth grade. To be honest I don't remember much about the tasks that were involved in being a patrol leader, instead I just remember that I wanted the role and was extremely happy to get chosen for it. I still have the special golden rope on my uniform to this day.

I did not have power when my biology instructor had me do a test on muscles  because I had to move to the next station as soon as he said "Move!". I felt rushed because I wanted more time to think about the questions.

My situation when someone had power over me, was when I was threatened to be nice to the person, and if i lashed out, they would tell my parents things that I didn't want them knowing. I felt vulnerable, and like I was stuck. I felt like a puppet.

When I was applying to college and meeting representatives I felt like I had no power. I knew that if the representatives liked me, then i would have a good chance and vise versa. Making a good impression was important, and i was extremely nervous.
Parents not approving of a study away trip for school, that it cost too much. In all my efforts to bring down the cost myself, they still were not satisfied. I felt rejected.

Whenever I am left alone with my younger cousins I am always the one in charge. I tell them what to do and tell them to stop doing something if they are doing something they shouldn't be doing. I like being in a position where I can provide a good example for my younger cousins. In these situations I usually feel proud of myself and I try to focus on being the best person I can be. My oldest younger cousin is about 13. The rest are a little younger than him.

As an athlete, I was put in leadership roles in high school. During track, I lead team warm ups and I was able to change it from day to day to ix things up but also prepare my team for a tough work out. It felt great knowing the coaches wanted me in that position. Having other athletes on the team who were just as deserving as I was made me feel special and that I was meant to lead.

When I gave my Senior Project presentation in high school. I had to give it to two faculty members and they were to evaluate me. My presentation was on animal testing and I was unsure where they stood on the topic. They had the power to give it  grade that would determine if I would graduate or not. I felt terrified. I was hyperventalating before I had to present and I kind of felt like I was going to throw up. The uncertenty of how they would grade me was nerve-racking.

When I was applying for a music scholarship all I was able to do was sing one song and then they determined whether or not I had enough talent to receive a scholarship that could determine if I ended up at PLU or not. All I could do was sing and then they talked for thirty minutes. They had complete power over my future at PLU just by hearing me sing once.

I worked at a daycare over the summer and was therefore in charge of many children. It was fun to be in charge but also difficult as the kids could be mean if they wanted something. Sometimes it was also difficult to know what to do in certain situations.

My senior year in high school, i had a B in english.  This doesn't sound too bad, except it was the first B that i had ever received.  The semester was coming to an end and i had to convince the teacher, who was notoriously stubborn with grades, to allow me to redo an assignment that i had done poorly on.  I approached her with my argument and supporting reasons as to why i should be able to re-do my paper, and the conversation began.  As i started to plea i felt my confidence waver as her face showed no emotion.  i began to feel desperate for other more convincing reasons to explain, but I drew a blank.  In the brief moment between the end of my speech and the beginning of her response i felt hope, intangible, ridiculously optimistic hope, but all the same it was hope and i clung to it.  She began to explain how it wasn't just for her to allow me to do something over when others could not.  I felt my heart drop, and just before i was about to leave, she offered a few point of extra credit.  It was just enough for me to get my grade up, but it required a lot of work.  At that point i thanked her so much and the next day i turned in the assignment and smiled proudly as saw my grade turn from an unimpressive B to a Beautiful A.  My GPA was saved.

A time in which I was in power was babysitting in my earlier teenage years. Babysitting grants you full power over the child in your care. You decide when they eat, what the play and any other daily activities. Yet, it gave me no sense of ultimate power over another being.

When I was working over summer at a fast food place the manager would boss me around to clean things for the 4 to 5 hours I would work.  I felt like i was useless and could be doing other more productive things that I actually wanted to do than just clean.

When I was in a position of power was when I was a captain for a soccer team two years in a row, captain for a fast pitch team, and captain for a basketball team. I felt like I had control and the reason why I was the captain was because I was the best, not only skillfully, but with my leadership. I am good at getting others what they want.
I was a part time swim coach teaching kids in the summer time.  I told them what swim sets to do and felt in control.
When I babysit my little brother. I do not particularly enjoy being in the position of power in most cases but I enjoyed it in this situation.

I did not have the power to say no to the demands of my choir teacher. In order to get a good grade in her class. I had to do everything she told us even if I did not like it. I could not change her opinions or attitudes abut things. She would not let us help her decide on music. I felt powerless, overwhelmed, insecure, frustrated and like she should not be in a position of power if she chooses to ignore the needs and wishes of those considered to be underneath her.

A position i did not have power in was after i tore my acl in basketball. My coach held all of the power over me because he decided my playing time and punishments for not doing as well as i had before my injury. It was frustrating and i felt powerless.
Presenting my senior project to two teachers. I had to fulfill their time requirement and score well on their rubric in order to pass and graduate from high school.

I was the captain of my volleyball team in high school. I felt like I always had to be doing the best I could so they wouldn't lose respect for me as their leader, I felt that I always had to be on time and play the best in the games. i also felt very supported and genuinely close to all of my teammates. That was our best season in the four years I played for my school- we had the least amount of drama, we went the furthest we had been, we had one of the best records in the league, and we were a really close team.
I was playing soccer, and a coach yelled at me for an incident that occurred. I felt pretty awful.
nothing happened to me like this. I'll not let anything like that happen to me.

I was class president for my graduating class in high school and it was stressful at times because I felt like sometimes I was the bad guy and could not please everyone. Teachers would also look at me for my responsibility.

The only situation I could think of was when I had to evaluate a group of students abilities in a science class I was mentoring for.  There were individual freshman students who I had to evaluate to see if they needed to start seeing tutors or staying after class to receive extra help.  Although most of the students did need the extra help I felt guilty for recommending they stay for the extra tutoring, and I did not feel very good about labeling them in that way. It is hard to label someone as "needs more assistance", because when they find out they realize that you, as the recommender, think they aren't meeting standards.
In high school teachers had power over you and were constantly evaluating how you did on tests and assignments. I felt normal because I grew up going to public school and that's just how it is.

When I was a student in high school, I was one semester away from becoming valedictorian. I needed to get a 90% on my chemistry presentation in order to maintain my A, and my teacher was a very tough grader. I knew that I could make a good presentation, but I was concerned that it would not be enough. I was scared and nervous and stressed out because I was so close to achieving the goal that I wanted to achieve, but I knew that after I did my presentation, I was no longer in control.

I was at soccer tryouts and the coaches were evaluating my performance, and I really wanted to make the team. I felt very nervous and anxious to do my very best that I could. I was nervous since I knew if I wanted a spot on the team my play would have to be nearly perfect.

I tend to feel extremely uncomfortable when someone holds power over me. Last night at work, we had a new manager and I was the sales associate who closed the store with her. She bossed me around do to tasks that were her responsibility, and then complained when I was unable to perform my tasks because I was doing hers. I was very frustrated and annoyed, and I have no idea how she was able to become a manager.
I played volleyball all throughout high school, and I always felt powerless over the judgement of the coaches watching silently during tryouts. I made the team every year, but I was still nervous.
today, i taught class. It was fun and I was thinking that I was looking forward to how the semester would go

I work at a movie theater so I have managers that are in charge of supervising, scheduling, and paying my coworkers and I. I never really questioned this authority because it never suited me to. From time to time my managers may have made a decision I disagreed with but it never was so extreme that I needed to bring it up with them. I've worked there so long that most of the managers that I have to listen to have less experience on the job than I do but I never applied for one of the positions because I knew that I would be leaving for college.

A few years ago, I was teacher in a religious ed. class for preschool and kindergarten. It was my responsibility to plan and execute lessons, evaluate individuals' performance, and change my plans to suit the needs of the group. It was a good experience, even though it was sometimes stressful. Sometimes, the students would want something I couldn't justify giving them (extra snacks, four drink breaks in a lesson, to play a game when we had to sit down for a story). Occasionally, I wondered if I was making the right decisions.

I was in control of my brother the other day and I felt confident because I am used to watching him, however, he was sick and when my brother gets sick he tends to throw up, and he has a bad gag reflex, so my feelings, emotions, and thoughts were on edge and a little worrisome. But, the weekend turned out to be fine and he stopped throwing up eventually. He was weak and sick, but still my happy little guy.

I lived with my mom who was financially unstable. Due to that I spent most of my time in high school working various jobs instead of enjoying experiences as a high school student; going to prom, joining the cheer team, spending time with classmates outside of school, etc. Yes, it was her problem by not working but it was also mine because I needed to make sure I had a roof over my head in order to continue to reach my goals of graduating high school, transitioning into college, and reaching career goals such as being a psychologist and having my own business one day. Because of the social standing of my mom I took into account the issues that were happening and they no longer became hers, they became ours and for that, she had power over me. I was not able to just pack my bags and leave while I was still in the middle of reaching my high school diploma. I felt trapped and hopeless. I felt like I was the adult while she was the child and that I was literally "13 going on 30" but in this sense, I was 16.

The first thing that comes to mind is team sports. Throughout high school, I was of the team captain for two of the sports I had played. The role of team captain requires a bit of power. Team captains are what keeps the team into the game and also keeps the team's drive for victory alive. I was the catcher for the high school softball team. Anyone familiar with softball or baseball knows that when it comes to where the ball is supposed to go; the catcher is the one to make the decision. Along with the power that is giving to these leadership roles comes some disagreements. Although there is no 'I' in team, sometimes players believer there is. This is where the role of team captain comes to play. So, in some ways team captains act as the mediator.

I once wanted to present a speech for my graduating class, but each student had to write their essay prior and submit it to win the speech. I was very confident in mine, and had wanted to write the speech for about two years. Once it was all said and done I did not win, but someone who I shared classes with and considered a friend won. He also beat me for vice president of a club at the beginning of the year, so I wasn't too surprised. I really wanted to present the speech, but I realized I didn't spend enough time writing it and focusing on it to deserve it. When he presented his, I was okay with not having won because his had the crowd laughing but also had a lot of sentiment in it that everybody enjoyed. He held me back from presenting, but he definitely deserved more than I did.

While working a night event at work I was left in charge by my supervisor to oversee the event and carry out my tasks. The opportunity was exciting as this was a fairly large event and being the supervisor was a fun test. I was selected because I was the most senior worker that was staffed that night although my fellow coworkers ranged from 19-25, I was only 17 at the time. The event ran smoothly and everyone carried out their responsibilities and had a good time. Afterwards, I felt good about the success and hoped I would get another opportunity. My boss was pleased wit how the event went and thanked me for doing it. All and all, it was good experience I think many teens miss out on.

I am in this position pretty often.  I was recently promoted to the hardest position at my job during the holiday season.  Because I was promoted to such an important position, I have to constantly be in power over them as well as constantly evaluate those individuals.  Being new to the job, my boss hired seasonal employee's, but now I am in a position where I need to constantly evaluate them in order to determine whether they stay post-holiday season, or if they are let go.  For one of my employees, I feel terrible because she says she is homeless, but she does not perform as well as she should if she wants to keep the job.  Therefore, I feel bad giving her a negative evaluation and letting her go after Christmas, but she shows negative behaviors by calling out often (usually on weekends,) using foul language, and being inappropriate in the work setting.

Teaching other students how to work with final cut pro x. In high school I taught younger students how to work a camera and how to edit footage. It does not bother me to have power or I feel as if I am to bossy. I enjoy being the leader in a team and I feel as if I have great leadership skills.

When it comes to fixing cars or anything such a man would do, people think, oh, you should tell your dad or your brother will take care of it. Many women are able to handle technical jobs. there are a lot of men who are incapable of such duties.
Interviewing for a job. They have to power to hire you or not. I was nervous but got the job.

One instance was when I played basketball. I really wanted to play and was really in the heat of the moment so I yelled at my coach. However, he ended up taking me out of the game, and at that moment I couldn't really do anything to get back into the game.

The last time I was in charge and had power was not too long ago.  I was a camp counselor for children.  I had to watch their every move and was responsible for them.  I loved my job because I love kids, but when they misbehaved I didn't like to punish them because I felt bad; although I know its what I had to do.  Overall, it was a great experience and I would definitely do it again.
When someone needed to borrow from me while we were shopping.  I was in power because if I were to not lend that person money then she would not have been able to purchase what she needed.

When  I wanted to buy something, like clothes or toys, and my parents said no. They had the power because of their authority and they had the money not me. I got mad because I couldn't get what I wanted.
One time I wanted to go out with my friends and my parents told me I couldn't go that night so I felt angry.

In the culture that I come from, women are thought of as weak and unable to fend for herself. Because of this boys will be given more freedom, than women, growing up. In m life I was never able to do a lot of things that my male friends could do, such going out. Every I asked my parents if I could do something their response would be a no and their reasoning was because I was a girl and I need to know my place. I was annoyed and angry whenever I heard that.
I told my mom if I could go to New York for thanksgiving break, but she didn't allow me to. Therefore, I could not go to New York and I was really disappointed and upset.

I cannot. at the moment, think of any situations that I felt someone had complete power over me in that sense. Though I have worked a places where it is mandatory that you had evaluations, to rank your performance and such. Even when I would get a perfect score, I still felt very uncomfortable. I felt like everything I had done in the last couple of months had been put under a microscope.

a time that I was in a pisiotno of power was when I had to fix a problem with the pipes in my basement and everyone was relying on my. I felt really good because people knew that I was the one from the job and that I could fix it.

I was interested in a girl that I was friends with and we started to get serious but she needed time and space to think things through and get to know me better. I didn't know how long it would take and what the outcome would be but she had more control over the situation than I did at the time. She wanted to evaluate me and see who I really am and even though I was positive I wouldn't do anything careless or destructive to the situation, I still felt like I was being put on the spot without much of a choice. I didn't like the feeling because it made me feel vulnerable and on edge.

When I shopping for my apartment, I wanted to get a small bed side table that I could use to put my alarm clock, makeup mirror, and etc., but my mom said I could not get it because my room was to small for it. I was extremely upset because she isn't going to be living in that room for a year, I have to. It is not like I was asking for an expensive table, but she wanted to buy me a whole bunch of unnecessary crap that I would never want.

Back when I was in high school, I was on my school's newspaper. The editor-in-chief had to read my articles and give me her feedback. Sometimes it was good, and other times it wasn't. She could be very critical, but only because she cared about making the newspaper as best as it could be. Whenever she criticized one of my articles I always felt disappointed in myself. I know I'm a good writer, but sometimes I felt like I wasn't. If she said I needed to change something, then I needed to change it. There really wasn't any arguing or debating with her. It made me feel like there was always something wrong with my writing or that I always made mistakes.

As a junior camp counselor a couple of summers ago, I was in charge of a group of 8 year old girls. I feel that having an eminence amount of power is dangerous because of the huge amount of responsibility for others. I feel that self-control is not always a factor when one has a lot of power because we has humans forget that, just because we can do something doesn't always mean that we should.  I knew that i had to make the right decisions for the safety of the campers but I will say that having a little bit of power is always somewhat thrilling.

In my job I am continually in the position of power due to my manager title. One instance was when deciding if an employee should receive a promotion, that situation was tough because it was dependent on my input.

my mother had power on me when i was younger. she was the one that made the final decisions in what i can and cannot have. At the time i would feel upset because i always wanted toys, but while growing up i had realize that i did not need the toys. i would just throw them away anyways.

An incident that I felt I was a position in power is when I did my summer job at my school and the children were being very loud and disrupted I told them if they do not stop talking then the instructor cannot do the next activity with them.  The children eventually stopped talking and when this happened I felt that I was respected and felt like a real authority figure.

I was in position of power when I had to evaluate an individual while completing tasks in school. While evaluating, I felt uncomfortable because I did not know the individual. I thought that maybe he was not taking me seriously because of the slight age difference, or maybe because we've never been acquainted previously.

I babysit my cousins sometimes. They are way younger them me so I can tell them what to do. I usually watch over them and give them lunch. They play and watch TV. I am just there to make sure that they do not harm themselves. he have become used to me and treat me as an adult. They do not cause much trouble but would sometimes feel a strong dislike towards me when I don't let hem do something because its harmful. They forget about it quickly but hey give me trouble and do not talk to me for a while. I can control their behaviors by threatening them with time out or no TV. They usually fix their behaviors then.

I was young and I was playing in the house. I broke my mother favorite mirror and my older brother saw. he promised not to tell only if I gave him half of my allowance every time. I remember feeling angry, but every time I tried not to give him my money, he threatened to tell my mother.

I was involved in a car accident and I was hospitalized for several weeks. While I was in the hospital, I couldn't do anything for my self so I had to depend on people around me to perform simple tasks for me. At the time I felt powerless and that made me miserable because I couldn't do anything for myself.

I was at a college softball camp where a lot of college scouts were examining how I play and if I was good enough to go to their school. It made me feel very nervous due to the fact that the event could dictate my future.

A situation where I didn't have any power was when I was working in a group project. Someone named themselves the leader of the group and told everyone what to do. During interviews usually he person who is interviewing you has the power over you. I felt very anxious and nervous. Even if I knew the answer I would not be able to answer it correctly.

I have taken care of an office before while my boss was gone to another country and the feeling of power is great. Actually taking charge felt amazing because you were able to do what you wanted if it felt right of course. I did not boss anyone around because that just seemed wrong but I was always helping people in other ways with their paperwork because they had to rely on me.

I was head of the costume theater department at Hollywood High. Everyday, my crew and I spent at least two hours organizing the clothes by color and style.  Organizing clothes everyday was not fun, but it was a nice feeling begin able to be in charge.

One situation that comes to mind was back in high school when I was the only person out of my group of friends who had a car and a license, so they had to ask me when they can go places and where they can go, unless their parents were able to take them. As a child you tend to desire many things, in my case my parents had the power to restrict me from obtaining certain desires I had. If i wanted a new toy I wouldn't always get it. At the moment I would feel disappointed, but would eventually get over it.

I was in a position of power when I took care of my little sister and cousin while our parents were either working or away. It was a fun experience though at times it did get stressful. Reasoning with children is sometimes hard because they just want what they want and do not like to listen to other people in moments of stubborness.
I wanted to purchase something from Target, and I just watched as the item I wanted was being picked up by someone that was not me. Mind you that item was the last one on the shelf.

As a teenager, my mom usually didn't give me as much freedom as others would have. When I wanted to do something, my mom usually had restrictions about letting me do it. At these times I usually felt like I was being treated unfairly compared to my friends or other teenagers.

When I was in high school, I had a position in Student Union. I had a instructor that I work for and follow on this position. An event would be when my roommate was able to get an iphone and i wasn't. I felt a little upset, but then i remembered its not always about material things.

I have never really had any incident where someone had power over me, but the closest was when I had my job interview. That loss of power made me very insecure about myself.

One time someone had power over me was when I was being told what to do by my teachers at my high school. I was not allowed to do what I wanted to do and had to follow their instructions. It made me unhappy that I had to listen to what they wanted, even if it disagreed with what I wanted.

My friend had taken my stuffed animal once so, I went to his dorm room to get it back. When I walked over to his room and demanded it back, I felt very empowered and intimidating. My friend seemed to be scared and I thought I had won and was going to get my stuffed animal back. I lunged at my friend to retrieve the toy, but when I did, he picked me up and carried me out of his room all the way back to my room at the opposite end of the hall. When this happened I felt extremely embarrassed and weak, especially because my friend is a very skinny and not particularly muscular individual. I had always liked to believe that I am stronger than I look, and this is true to an extent, but when someone is able to physically lift my entire body off the ground, it makes me feel like I have no control and I do not like it, it makes me feel weak, and acts as a major hit to my pride.

I was applying for a stocking position at Costco Wholesale. I decided to not work there because I became afraid that the job was not adequate for me.

The situation I recall in which I was in a position of power was in high school's anime club. I was the treasury of that time. The reason why I think I was in power at that time is I believe I have the authority over the club's financial flow and provide accurate data for the club's operation. I felt that the club members depended on me and it made me become more reliable to them. By having power, I think it is a way for me to establish a closer relationship and friendship with my team.

I often tutor people. In such events, I lead discussions relevant to the lecture material. I tend to use different methods of teaching to make sure the student is fully aware of the information and is capable of applying it. It makes me feel as though I have some value beyond my existence. I appreciate it when people look up to me, in fact, I thrive off those experiences. I am a very insecure person, so instances in which I have control reassure me of my competence and intelligence.

As a child, my parents always had power over me. I remember wanting a toy from the toy store and they refused to buy. In event in which I was in a position of power was when I had to evaluate the essays of my peers in High school. It comes to say that when one is in a position of higher power, even if its only slightly, one still feels like they have much power over the rest- in my case other students.

It was a group project and I was the leader of the project. I need to assigned tasks for each group members in order to finish the project. Being the leader did not feel good because you were responsible to most the situations in the project. However, when the project was finished and came out well, I did feel satisfied.

Growing up I have always been the child to cry to get what I wanted from my parents. It is frustrating at times but over time I let it go.
I used to organize a graduation party when I graduated for the high school. At that time, my all classmates followed my steps. Then, they said they were enjoy it.

I felt intimidated and as if everyone was watching for every single mistake that I made.
When someone ends a relationship you have to accept it. You have no power over it. I was sad.

Someone that had control over my ability to get something that I wanted was my dad at some point, when he was basically telling me I could not go to a college that I personally wanted to go to, that he'd make the decision for me, otherwise he wouldn't pay for my education.  I felt very limited and that he didn't support me.

The Beyonce and Jay Z concert was coming to a city near me so I purchased 2 tickets. The first person i knew would love to go was my little sister Isaura. I told her that if she finished her semester with at least all B grades she would be able to go so she worked harder and came home with As and Bs versus the Ds Cs and Fs she had come with from the previous semester. I felt that i had power over her school performance.

A situation which someone had power over me was my former store manager.  She was a very mean, unhappy, and rude individual.  Instead of guiding the company to succeed as a team, she always tried to dictate the employees to show that she is "the boss".  Even when she was wrong, she never admitted to it.  How I felt in such situations were not the best feelings.  I felt upset, irritated and simply disturbed to be working with such an arrogant individual.  Just because one is the boss does not mean that they know everything.  One must attain a growth mindset, and simply remain learn able because at the end of the day, there is nothing more beautiful than improving ones self and learning.  I know that I have a voice, and I am very opinionated, and the fact that one made me feel like I do not have a voice got me feeling very disgusted towards them.  At the same time it built my character because it made me realize that in life we are always going to meet individuals who are not going to be our cup of tea, but we can not control who they are.  What we can control is how we react and act to situations.  I came to the understanding that one day I will move on with my life and excel to greater things, and one day when I become a doctor, I will not treat my workers as if they do not have a voice.  A leader is not one who tells the ship to sail, rather one who guides them through the journey.

A time I was in a position of power was when I was able to assist my manager considering new hires for our store. I have always known that money is power. That opinion is shared by my current World Politics teacher of UC Riverside as well. I was on the varsity basketball team for four years during high school and my coached made me co-captain. Every single game I had to lead the team into warm ups, huddles, and the pre game pep talk. no incident comes to mind
While I was working for the student recreation center at UCR as a weight room attendant, I applied to be a personal trainer. My bosses had power over weather they would hire me as a trainer.

I was Color Guard Captain when I was in high school and during our Finals championships performance, I motivated my peers and fellow marching band friends about making the best out of our last performance of the show. When my cousin was looking for a job, I had connections so I introduced her to a job she would be most likely be interested in. I am satisfied with my experience there.

I was babysitting my younger cousin, who was four at the time. He kept wanting to play with all my stuffed animals but he was making a mess of my room so I told him to stop and put them away. He did as I had told him. I wouldn't say that I felt an extreme amount of power over him, to be honest it didn't really cross my mind at the time. I was just pleased that I could find something else for him to do that kept him happy and essentially kept me happy because my room was no longer a mess.

A time where someone had power over me was when I was caught dating someone who was older than me by a few years. It was either to keep dating him and be happy, or live with the continuous disappointment of my parents. I didn't know what to do. I was lost.

Like many other moms, my mom often has power over me. One of the many incidents is when she wanted me to take AP classes in high school. I knew that I was not ready but i didn't have any choice because she is my mother and I don't like to go against her. I felt troubled and pressured knowing what i would have to so if I take those difficult classes.

My dad uses power over me frequently in order to get me to do what he wants me to do. He pays for a lot of things for me, so if I am acting in a way he does not want me to act he will cut me off from his money supply. I have no choice but to comply with him because I cannot afford to live on my own and I do not qualify for financial aid because of his income.

Whenever I needed something from my younger brother whether it was a favor or money I felt like I could get what I wanted from him because I was older and bigger than him therefore I felt more power. I knew that it was wrong to sometimes threaten him, but hey I had the power and I usually got what I wanted from him which felt a bit pleasing at most, but of course not through violence just words.

The last time I felt someone else had power over me was when I participated in a research study and I was told to follow certain rules. I cannot recall any particular moment in my life in which someone has had power over me, in which they controlled my ability to get something I wanted. I am sure there are some but I cannot recall any of them and by that reasoning the must not have been very important.

There was a presentation I had to do for English where I had stuttered and stumbled over my words. I felt judged and helpless, but I had to finish presenting what I had. In the classroom, the teachers have a power over me and decide what grade I get in the future.  To get on the teachers good side, I did all the work I was supposed to, but didn't like having to do work.

I do this almost everyday in my line of work. I work as a DSP (Direct Support Professional) for the mental disabled so I am constantly in a position of power. Being a position of power is normal to me, but is gratifying in a sense that I helping them to help themselves in hopes that they learn and develop proper social norms and basic safety skills.

I work in retail, thus I come across many frustrating customers that try to have it their way. I have the power to authorize or decline any merchandise returns. People often try to return items that have been worn or try to save as much money as possible. I get annoyed by them very easily. Last fall during college application and admission time. This made me feel very nervous and anxious as I wait for the results of my college admissions.

I felt like I was in control all the time and also felt like that none of the kids could tell me what to do. I thought that I could also control how the children were feeling since I would have the ability to tell them what to do and what not to do .

A time when someone had power over me was when my little brother attempted to "blackmail" me. He told me that if I didn't do what he said, then he would try to get me in trouble with my parents. I felt fearful.

I felt powerless because there was nothing I could do to bring this criminal to justice because I am just a teenager. When I was buying my house, the bank had power over me in deciding whether or not I would be able to buy the house. They made the ultimate decision whether to loan the money to me or not. It was a stressful situation but in the end it was worth it all because I was able to buy my house.

I recall myself in a position of power when I was chosen team captain of the soccer team years ago. The title itself made me feel strong and just overall powerful. I felt that I was the one who could do orders and tell my team what to do and what not to do. It was a nice feeling, at the fact that I was the one in control.

I really wanted to get a car that I liked since I am commuting to school, but my dad just got me a different one that he liked but I disliked. In a class we had to fill out a form about who participated in the group project and how much work they put in. There is always one person who depends on the rest of the group to do the work. The most recent incident of someone having a certain amount of power over me, was that of my parents. They have power over my financials as well as my housing. It made me feel good, considering they were my parents and they had the authority to do that, and they helped me in any way possible.

My older brother and I are four years apart. Ever since I could remember, he would bully me or abuse his power over me when my parents were there. I didn't have to make much decisions in my early life.

Being a tutor I need to follow the orders of my supervisor. In these situations I felt fine because it was part of being a tutor, so did not mind it at all.

I cant recall a specific incident in which I felt in power. I think anytime someone is emotionally involved with anything you say or do, you become in power.

I was forced to help out with my family's rental unit company. My father, the owner and the person who managed every part of the company, continually left my brother and myself alone for several hours to paint a condo, tear out carpet or laminate flooring or other similar task. I was never excited for helping out with these jobs but they helped pay for school supplies and tuition. As long as i had the tools to do the job, some form of music to listen to and extra cash for emergencies i was content. After several years the business took a toll on all of the family so we all agreed to get outside help from are Realtor to help manage the rental units.

Interviews to obtaining a position as a sales associate at a retail store. I wanted the job, and I was being evaluated for it. The owners of the store were the mediators and decided if I should have the job or not. I got the job and I was very grateful, but prior to that, I was anxious.

When I was being judged by my middle school teacher because she did not like my attitude. I did something that seemed disrespectful to her which made her comment various things about me that were unpleasant

The club that i am participating had a pool and bbq party yesterday. I was told to prepare food and supplies for the event. I was excited because i could get involved and in charge with the event. I feel like i got the power to hold the event.
As part of an internship, I always had a superior. Someone who told me what to do throughout the day. I didn't like being told what to do constantly.

I really wanted to go to Las Vegas with an aunt and my parents refused to give me permission. Even though I really wanted to go, they said I couldn't go without giving me a good reason why and that made me really angry.

I was a Sunday school teacher at my local church. I had to do what was best for them and not what was best for me. I didn't like having power. I would have rather been alone and not have to deal with the responsibility.

the last time i was in a position of power was during a class last quarter. We had to evaluate our partners in a project and that evaluation would count for 1/3 of the project grade. I felt the need to put that people participated even if they did not do very much.

I overall liked having some power though.

There was an item that I wanted to get, but someone was preventing me from doing so, and his reason was simply because "he didn't want me to have it." It made me angry at first because he was being pretty unreasonable but after a while, because I didn't care about the item that much, I didn't care anymore.

I was in power when i controlled what candies my cousins would receive. It felt good to be able to control their fate in a way. I felt like i was superior to them. However I did feel guilty when not all of my cousins were satisfied with my choices.

As an athlete, coaches have always had some power over me. Especially during high school varsity football, my coaches evaluated my performance on the practice field which would result in certain amounts of playing time during actual games. I felt apathetic towards the situation, as I just put my head down and worked my absolute hardest to get as much playing time as I could to help my team win.

Everyday as students attend school we are in a position to be evaluated all the time; from our peers, our mentors, our professors, our families - students are under the magnifying glass every day.  This is a position we willingly put ourselves to gain a competitive edge in today's market and educational setting.  We take pride in our work and know that the very brightest and well connected of us will go on to do great things, but space is limited at the top.  This is why students are always evaluating each other and themselves.  This is to prepare us for the time in which professors or those with actual power over us will begin to decide which of us is the best and succeeds.  This can be exhausting.  I recall that in my various psychology and math classes I was stretched so thin that I was snapping at others for their mistakes that I thought should not happen at this level of education.  When the time came for me to be evaluated, I doubted myself and my abilities. This was the moment I had been studying for throughout my academic career.  I took every mistake I committed on that test as a personal blow to both my pride and against the teacher who had so diligently and patiently molded me from my beginnings as a student to the point of being awarded a certificate.  While I had passed, I strived to do better. To make my family, my teachers, my fellow classmates, my friends, my community proud. I knew that my professors did not have anything personal against me, they were just doing their job. I appreciated them for that and hold no ill will against them.

When I was little I always wanted a airsoft gun. My parents promised they would buy me it if I get all A's. I got all A's on my report card but then my parents said it was dangerous. I was very angry!

I was at work and I was told to train a new employee. I felt superior knowing I knew so much and another person didn't. It was rewarding to know that a person is paying close attention to what I do and say.

In high school, I turned in my final report for English and my English teacher evaluated it. At the time, he looked at me and laughed, stating, "I'll have fun grading this". I felt a little apprehensive and anxious at his tone, feeling as if he would give me a bad grade and fail me in his English class. However, I felt as if I had given the final report my best shot and was not too worried; all I knew was that the fate of my AP English grade rested in his hands. I ended up receiving an A- on the paper.

In eleventh grade i was the leader of my history group project. At the end of the presentation I got to give each person a grade. The grade I gave counted as one fourth of their overall grade. I felt powerful but I wanted to give grades that would allow them to pass the class.

I was left in charge of my little brother for a few hours while my parents went out grocery shopping. I had told him earlier that week that I would take him to the park to play with his friends. The moment my parents left he asked if we could go. I however, was not feeling up to taking care of a whole bunch of little kids so I told him no. And he was upset and begged me to take him. I got so irritated that I told him that I wouldn't, and that he'd better stop bugging me about it or he wouldn't get to watch T.V. He finally did leave me alone and after ten minutes or so I started feeling bad for being so mean to him and I ended up taking him to the park anyway.
Interview.  People can decide whether or not you get the job.  I felt pressured, but did not show it.

The last time I remember someone having this power over me was my mother. She had taken away my car due to personal reasons but I felt completely shocked and hopeless and didn't know what to do because I've had my car since I was 16.
At an arcade, when I wanted this particular prize, I had to get up to a certain amount of points to get it, but I wasn't able to. I wasn't able to get what I wanted.

In high school, I was heavily involved in student government. Every year, I interviewed students interested in joining and my evaluation of them had a heavy input in determining whether or not they would be able to join student government. I liked my position as president of student government because I like to be in control of situations, but I also understand that a leader needs to be someone people can trust, admire, and be inspired by. Many times, I would interview students and my questions made them nervous, but I did my best to create a relaxing environment so they wouldn't need to feel pressured to say the "right" thing.

When I was interviewed by a board consisting of four people for a scholarship, I remember how they were judging and evaluating everything I said.  I definitely felt nervous about the whole situation, yet I also felt confident because I enjoy talking in front of others.
I got grounded and my mom took everything away from me. She basically decided what i was allowed to watch, do, etc. I felt very vulnerable.

I was at work and I work at the Scottys at AI and I am usually very excluded from everyone since its a little off of the rest of the dining hall. I cannot leave my station unless I have someone else come and take over the register. I called in that I was missing some items and the manager told me he would come and get me some soon. I waited and waited until finally someone came in to give me my break and I told them. They asked me if i could do it after my break was done. I felt very useless because I couldn't do it myself, I have to wait for other people and for the most part since I am so far away that I am often forgotten about.

I was a person of power when I had to be the mediator between my best friend and his girlfriend. They asked me who the right one was in a specific situation they had. I felt like there was no real right answer because both sides had valid points.

When I am at a baseball showcase I do not have any power on whether certain colleges will offer me a scholarship or if I will even be able to make the team. I know I can play but it is just up to the coaches to determine if they think that I can play. I felt like I didn't have much control and that they had the power to make any decision that they wanted to.

When i was employed, the managers would make me do the bottom of the food chain tasks such as sign spinning, and keep me for hours after i was scheduled off with no over time pay. I felt powerless and to this day still regard that as some of the worst experiences of my life.

Just a few weeks ago. Academic adviser put a hold on my account for a misunderstanding on their part regarding what grade as was in. Despite fulfilling the tasks that were given to me, they forgot to remove the hold and therefore, resulted in the delay of my registering. Feeling of annoyance as they put the blame on me for not communicating properly despite have been sent emails directly after finishing the task and before my registration.

I was the captain of my soccer team and I was able to help my coach decide whether or not they should be put on the team. During tryouts my coach would ask me how I felt about certain players and I would tell him whether they were good or bad. I helped control something that these players wanted very badly and it gave me a lot of power and I liked the feeling.

In high school, I was the group leader of a big science project. I believe I was in a position of power because I was the one responsible to assign what each member would contribute in and make sure we all put appropriate effort in our work to get a good grade in our project. It felt good to be the group leader, but at time it was frustrating.

In high school, I was a member of the student government and I conducted interviews for other students that wanted to be apart of student government. I along, with my advisor, were deciding which students would get a spot or not.

In 2012 I found myself face to face with a professional musician to perform my physical playing part of my CM certificate of merit for cello. I was given the piece beforehand but the musician kept telling me to switch between pieces and only asking me to play certain parts of the songs. He also told me to do on the spot sight-reading and playing. It felt unnerving because he never showed any form of emotion. He just stared straight at me, analyzing my entire performance to the minute details. I also felt very self-conscious, thinking that every little mistake I made would be the one that resulted in me not passing the evaluation.
my parents wouldn't let me eat ice cream one time. i was sad and didn't understand why they wouldn't let me.

A situation in which i did not have power would be the time where I was not able to get into a class I really needed in order to transfer, that was up to the professor at the time and where or not he would allow me to add the class. I felt a sense of exasperation, frustration, anger, and sadness. I remember feeling helpless, like there was nothing I could do and something that was important to my academic success was relying on the decision of a professor who could probably care less about my personal issues. The fact that there was a possibility I might not have been able to transfer was enough to stress me out and make me want to cry. In the end I was able to get into the class, and all those negative mixed up emotions turned into relief, happiness, and gratitude.

In high school, we had teachers who were very strict. They wouldn't let us do anything without their approval first. One time, I wanted to walk with this underclassmen to their class, because it was the first day of school and they had no idea where they were going. The teacher who was supervising my class, saw it as a way for me to skip parts of lecture instead of me helping a friend. I couldn't help the new person and that person was late to all their first classes. It made me feel weak that I couldn't stand up to a teacher, because then it would be my butt in detention for this one kid. But then I was angry when I found out that the kid was late to every single class. It wouldn't have taken that long to escort them or draw a detailed map. I felt bad and from that point on that 'kid' is a really close friend.

I recall having an interview for a job I applied to and the manager who was interviewing me was grilling me with questions and seeking out specific responses which gave me the feeling that he was more looking into stressing me out that actually hiring me. I felt powerless and could not find any way to get myself out of the situation than just to walk up and leave

A time when I had the ability to control a person's thoughts was when a friend gave me their full trust and told me all their inner thoughts. His full trust in me felt like a burden because anything I say would some how brain wash his thinking. I was able to evaluate his life from his point of view and give feedback from my point of view. It made me feel powerful, yet, scary in so many ways because I had the ability to be right all the time. It didn't matter if I was wrong or right, he believed what I said, and attempted to live out my words. The ability to brainwash someone seems wrong to me because they begin to live out your words instead of their own life.

There was one time when my roommate's glasses lost a screw and she asked to help her find a way to fix it because she couldn't see clearly without them. I didn't have any particular feelings about the situation except probably sympathy because she won't be able to get new glasses or get them fixed properly until she goes home. I just wanted to help her find a temporary remedy and I ended up taking a small flexible piece of metal to help hold her glasses together. I felt accomplished after and I was happy to be able to help.
I had the position of choosing where me and my friends were going to go eat. It was late at night, and I was hungry for something warm and spicy. I then decided we were going to Buffalo Wild Wings.

i used to work in administrative service of a local hospital, and had to go department to department to address patient complaints. i was very dissatisfied of the job because it was difficult dealing with every individuals' problems, and having to come up with a solution while worrying about the outcome of the situation (whether it complied to hospital rules and regulations). i felt stressed!

At work, I have once helped the manager evaluate how a new cashier was doing on her first days of work. My thoughts were to be honest about how she was doing her job, her weaknesses and strengths, and emphasizing the positive things about her work.

I was a judge in a performing arts  program.  I was in the position of power because I was the one who decided which person would play which role in a play.  I felt really empowered, as if everyone's fate were in my hands.  I felt respected as well, since everyone wanted to get on my good side, hoping that I would  be more lenient on them, if they were to perform badly.  The position of power made me feel good.

I was captain of my high school's drill team and would always run practices over with my team mates. It was my position to push them to reach their fullest potential and that meant ignoring the fact that these people were also my friends. I had to separate my duty as a leader and as a friend. I remember recruiting members during try outs and a few of my friends would try to join along. The decision was made primarily by me, my co-captain, and coach. However, it was hard because some of them didn't meet the standards that were set. So I had to play the bad guy and break it to them that they didn't pass the rounds. It hurt to know that they really wanted something and I had the power to give it to them, but I wanted to be a leader that was unbiased and uninfluenced by connections and other outside factors. I'd rather have a person obtain something through hard work and dedication rather than not really caring at all.

I was on a committee to elect the next president of a club. I had to read their essays about why they wanted to lead and club and evaluate each one to pick the best candidate. I felt pressured and unsure about my capabilities but in time became confident about my decision.

I remember that when I was working as a lifeguard, there were many patrons who wanted to take control over me because I was 18 while most of them were about 30 years old. They weren't very respectful of what I do because of my age compared to the other lifeguard who worked there. I remember feeling like I wasn't that great of a lifeguard or I couldn't handle this but then I knew that I am the one who's certified and is going to get in trouble if they didn't follow my directions. I took control of the situations and let them know that I was in charge and I'm the person who's looking after them if an incident is to happened. The patrons seemed a bit angry but then they got over it as they saw how dedicated of a lifeguard I am. I remember feeling powerful and assertive as I let them know that age doesn't matter and I am their superior when they're in the pool.

back when I was in high school, everyone in the school had to attend a mandatory meeting every morning. One day, during a meeting I was having some stomachache and asked to leave the meeting for a moment but the professor refused my request, thus forcing me to say in the meeting for long time. I was quite offended by this since I cannot control my own biological need and I believe I had a good reason to leave the meeting.

I was in charge of training a new employee that would be taking my position within the company, after I had left. It was my job to train him on everything that I knew. It was in my hands to train him in the way that I wanted him to be trained, and at what pace he was trained. By the end of the time that I had to train him, he still was not as ready as I would of liked him to be. He was learning the information too slowly for my liking, and his lack of enthusiasm bothered me. Before leaving the company, I was able to relay this information back to my manager. I knew that this would not get him fired, but that this would definitely warn my manager to be aware of this progress.

My mother recently signed me up for catechism at a local church. She did not tell me and paid the fee. I felt bad because she paid money so I decided to attend. She always tells me that I am an adult now and have to make my own decisions, but I feel that I do not have the power to decide for myself. I feel disappointed because she made me do something I was not advised of.
Blackmail. I remember my peers would threaten to "tell the teacher" what I did unless I did certain things.
When I was looking for apartment for this quarter, my mother interfered with my decision. I felt angry because the suggestion she gave me no sense.

It was yesterday when I wanted to get off work at 2:30. I went to tell the head hostess that I was going to get off work but she decided to tell me to stay till 3 because there were still customers in the restaurant. I didn't feel anything until I was asked to describe this description. But now, I feel as if I didn't have any say in when I would get off even when it has been a set schedule.
I've never been in a position of power where I had control over something that someone wanted in an obvious way.  I can't think of anything.

When I was younger my cousins would mess around with me and take my toys. I was around 8 years old at the time. Two of my cousins were older and one was younger. The younger was was 6 years old. One time they took my toy and tossed it between the three of them. I recall grabbing my toy back from my youngest cousin. He tried to resist and I ended up punching him in the face. After that incident my cousins stopped taking my belongings from me

I definitely felt that my band director had power and control over me when I was part of my high school's concert and marching band. He would hold evaluations at least twice a month where he would examine out ability to play the music for that week as well as evaluate how well we could read rhythm and "sight read". He had control over the music, the choreography for the show and the activities that the band had to do. I certainly didn't agree with him on everything he chose for me. For example, he demoted and promoted me in terms of whether I was first or second chair several times and he also chose not to name me drum major. My reaction was that of frustration, but I tried to keep it to myself since I knew that he had much more experience in this field than I did.

As a past sales associate at Juicy, I helped and listened to customers to see what it is exactly that they wanted, related to clothing, or dresses for an event that they were looking for. I had to first ask them what they had in mind then I would help them find it and make sure it was what they wanted. I was in control since I was working at that store and they were shoppers coming in. I had to also pay attention to some customers more than others because they were frequent shoppers and I already knew their personality more than the others.
I persuaded my friend Annie to let Jenny come over. I was in position because I was really close to Annie. Jenny isn't as close to us but we felt bad for her.

I play a goal keeper in soccer, and I think that is a position of power because you are the head of the team, you have to direct people where to go and you help control the game. So the way I controlled the ability of other people to get something they wanted is by guiding the team to winning.

An incident in which I was in a position of power was when I had to babysit. The kids could not do much without asking. I would decide when it was time for them to eat and when it was time for them to sleep. When dealing with kids there is a feeling of exhaustion along with power because they look up to you and listen to you most of the time.

I wanted to go out that night with friends and my significant other was upset that I wanted to do this. He manipulated me by making me say I would not go and I ended up staying home. I felt sad because he had ruined my night and on top of that did not even want to talk to me.

The situation was when i was a cashier at CVS and a woman said that i had not given her the correct change. i could have given her the money, ten dollars, that she claimed to be owed, but i knew that i had given it to her already and was not going to give in to her demands. I refused to give her the money and then called my supervisor up to handle the situation. I knew right away that I had given the money to her and that she was trying to deceive me because from the moment she walked in, i knew that she would not be a quiet customer. She walked in and shouted a question to me, which annoyed me because it was rude to shout and because i was with another customer. She then took one of the sample spray bottles and sprayed it all over herself, and then carried it with her across the store. I distrusted how she looked and acted and was sure that she was going to steal it. When she lied to me about the money, i was almost willing to give in but i was not going to be blamed for being ten dollars short in my drawer. I was also about to give her a refund for the eggs she had bought but i knew that giving her a little of what she demanded would not please her entirely and could cause her to demand more. I was scared she would do something drastic and that is why i called up my supervisor. Also, i had only been working there for about a month or so and I did not want my inexperience to show, should she take advantage of that.

The time I was in a position of power was when I decided whether or not my sister could buy the item she wanted. At that time, I just thought that she didn't need it, nor was it any use in the future. I didn't want her to spend money on things that will not be used in the future, especially since we were financially struggling.

In recalling a situation in which someone was in a position to evaluate me I can hardly remember. But in that kind of position it would be with teachers who are watching from the back as they are grading you on how well you did on an oral presentation either by your self or with a group. I do not do well speaking in front of the class as I always get really nervous getting up there. In fact one time in a group presentation I could barely talk even though I had my note cards up there. In another class I was still nervous and still stuttered through my part but it was better than the other class i was in. I like to believe that it's the feeling of everyone staring at you is what makes me feel small and nervous every time I have to go up front of the class.

I'm not particularly interested in being in a position of power. However, I once was the "leader" of a group project. If anything, it was a stressful task having to make sure everyone did what they were supposed to.

Back in the day. I was leading a class of forty students. I found the experience to be rather stressful, and I felt a responsibility to profile the best instruction and guidance for the long term success of my students despite their resistance. I believed the resistance was due to the lack of instant gratification and in retrospect the majority of my students surpassed their peers in other classes, and became successful individuals.

I really wanted this internship at a hospital, however it was extremely difficult to get into. There were a series of 10 hour training days, a practical (hands on) exam and a written test. Although there wasn't a physical person holding power over me, they were evaluating me at every step of the way. Needless to say, I did pass the exams and got the internship.

For the last half of my senior year of highschool, I was an aide at a physical therapy clinic. I spent a lot of time helping elderly people with their necessary rehab. One day, one of my patients stopped breathing and I performed CPR and got his heart beating again.

Every day at work I feel in a position of power. Working in costumer service gives me the ability to contribute to the needs of the costumers. I have the authority to decide whether some transactions will be made or if the costumes will get his money back for a returned item.

In high school i partook in a debate against a male that believed that men are more powerful than women. However, i was able to win the argument do to the fact i was well prepared and i knew the topics he was going to bring up. Knowing his topics allowed me to have power because i was able to have counter examples. In this way i never gave him a chance to fully argue. I felt strong and accomplished because i was prepared. I showed him that women are just as powerful as men.
I do not wish to disclose the details of the situation, but, emotionally, I felt powerless, trapped, unable to successfully communicate my ideas and what I thought about the situation.

Growing up as the youngest in the family, I was constantly ignored because they believed my opinions were inferior due to the gaps in age. One experience I remember in particular was when I was expressing my aspirations about the career I wanted to pursue to my oldest sister. I wanted to participate in a program, similar to an internship for said the career. She told me that when I would get older, that I'd get over that passion because it required a great amount of intelligence. She relayed her opinions to my mother who then decided that she didn't want me to attend the summer program because it wasn't profitable in her eyes, and thought I'd be better off getting a summer job in retail. Not having my mother's consent at 14 made me feel very unhappy to say the least because everyone believed I couldn't grow up to accomplish more than my siblings had. Although it crushed my spirits at the time, as I got older I constantly reflected on that experience and it empowered me to pursue that career choice.
