To this day I am still pursuing it, for my own satisfaction and to prove them wrong.

I recently got into an accident with a semi-truck and had to go through an attorney to make my claim against the truck company. I was told to go to the doctor and get evaluated, do MRI scans, and see a physical therapist due to back problems. I also had to record how severe my pains were so that it can be used in the case. I felt like everything I did I was being evaluated because if my case was not that severe then the money I get back from the truck company would be less than if I was in severe pain. I went through a process of questions and evaluation and it just felt overdone because I couldn't just voice my opinion, I had to gather up evidence of pain or problems relating to my health.

It was 8th grade and my math grade wasn't doing as well as it normally would, and due to the fall in the grade my teacher called my mother. He informed her that i wasn't doing my homework and that i wasn't going to pass the class. When my mom found out she was extremely angry at me and forced me to work on my grade more. I passed the class with a C+ but the teacher wasn't happy that i passed it without doing half of the homework for the semester. He called my mom again and they agreed to make me retake Geometry in high school even though i had passed. I felt like i was robbed since i did the work to pass, and I didn't get anything out of it. It angered me that they would freely control my future because i didn't pass the class, the way they wanted me to.
When i became involved with someone I gave them power over me. I felt angry with myself for putting myself in such an awful position, frustrated, hurt, and helpless.

As a lifeguard, a swimmer wanted to jump of the diving board but the diving board isn't open during lap swimming hours. The swimmer started using vulgar language and was very disrespectful. With the authority of being a lifeguard, I told the swimmer that if he didn't listen to me, I would have to bring out my supervisor and ask him to leave. The swimmer obeyed my authority and got out of the pool. I felt good because I reinforced the right thing. I politely told him the consequences and he listened.

When I was the captain of the wrestling team, I had the power to lead the team during drills, stretches, warm ups, and more. Though I had the power to get the wrestling team to follow whatever I instructed, I did not see myself above anyone else. The leadership given to me was a way to guide and help improve the team in every aspect possible. My leadership was used to organize and keep the team focused. When the wrestlers would want a break, I'd tell them to continue wrestling. Though the teammates did not agree with my decision at the moment, they later realized that it was more beneficial in the long run. My team chose me as a captain for a reason, and although I had the leadership and responsibility, I did not consider myself to be greater than anyone else in the team.

An instance where I felt like I did not have power was at my job, when I saw something some outside the front counter occurring that was unpleasant but had no right to say anything. The manager was there, visibly able to see what was happening but did nothing. At that point I felt the urge to do something to or at least comment for maybe some self reflection of the person committing the action but I knew I needed the job. I felt so trapped.

It feels rather easy to manipulate people growing up, but later on in life, they get wiser. Nowadays, there are people who let you in on their lives or become vulnerable for a moment. I met some first year UCR students, who wanted to explore what Riverside had to offer. They couldn't decide what to do, so I just asserted we can go eat and have drinks back at the dorms. Once everyone was drunk, they became easy to evaluate on what kind of person each were or who will they become. I avoided drinking that night and was able to keep a clear mind. They say a drunk person's talk is a sober person's thoughts. I was able to see who I can trust for the remainder of the years at UCR, who would be the "party animal", the alcoholic, studious person, and the natural smart person who didn't have to try to earn good grades. I was able to evaluate these individuals so I can choose who want to stay friends with and have a good four years at UCR.

During a group project in my English class a few years ago, i took on the role of writing a script for the project. During that time, i would assign the roles of the other three members of my group to find important events from novels so that i may integrate those short stories into the script. I enjoyed writing the script as i controlled the information that would be fed to me so that i wouldn't have to research it myself. Also, no one complained about the positions they would have to act in the script as it made the story line better.
Actually, I do not have the memory of i was in the a position of power.

The last time someone had power over me was when my friend didn't let me take a 10 minute nap. I felt a little stubborn and mad. Even though I was upset at my friend, I knew she was just trying to help me out in the end.

My last incident in which I was in power was when I was recruiting possible members to become a part of my group organization. I felt very calm, however, I assume that the person I was questioning was a bit nervous.

Before I came to UCR at my job I was a trainer. I was in charge of training the workers and deciding if they would be promoted. I sometimes loved my job and sometimes I didn't. Having power can be good and bad because sometimes it can change a person. I didn't always like having power because of the amount of responsibility that came with it. I had to make sure I was always on top of my job because people were watching me, I also had to do things I didn't want to do because it was my job.

There was a situation in the work place where I wanted to do a particular assignment in a different way. I thought it would be more effective to do the particular task one way that didn't take a lot of effort and would be a quick solution to the issues that continually arose. My supervisor made it very clear that we had to do the task in this manner with no explanation to why. I felt very powerless and frustrated because my supervisor negated my opinion as well as my co-workers in a manner that demeaned us. I felt uncomfortable and demeaned especially because our opinions and insight were ignored.
I felt powerless when I was being choke as training for my Judo class. Although I knew that I could get my partner to stop at any time, it was a terrifying aspect when I felt my oxygen cut off.

A course that i took last quarter we were put into groups of five and we had to do a presentation together. Two members in the group did no work at all and we had to pick up the slack. The TA had the power to do something, but did nothing. She simply told us to work together. My grade was depending on the presentation and on my team and i did not have the power to get the two members to work or get out of the team, i felt frustrated and annoyed.

As a close friend of the president of one of the clubs I used to frequent, I was given the responsibility of evaluating the possible candidates for certain club officer positions. I arranged meetings with these candidates and interviewed them. Then I decided which ones were suited to become officers in the coming year and which ones had to go. As I was doing this, I felt respected.

We had to write an essay in my honors class. The professor had mentioned that he didn't want the class to be as strenuous as previous honors classes had been. He went against what he told us in the beginning and assigned a 5-page paper due the same week as midterms. I e-mailed him and asked him why he was going against what he told us in the beginning of the year. His reply was something to the effect of "you're an honors student, you should be able to manage your time." It made me feel powerless, I ended up writing a 4-page paper that I'm not too proud of.

Last year, I had saved up enough money to buy a new phone, and I had already found the one I wanted. I told my dad that I was going to buy it, but he said that he was not going to let me buy it. He said he didnt like that phone, so I could not get it. I felt upset because I was very excited to get a new phone with my own money, which I had saved up for years. I was dissapointed because i was not able to do what I wanted to do. I had no power over my actions of getting a phone.
I was in charge of two younger siblings while away. I felt like they had to listen to me and ask me if they were hungry or needed anything.

When I was in high school I played baseball, I was captain of the team and was able to control what we did for practice when ever our coach didn't show up I had the authority to decide whether we even practiced or not, I controlled how much we ran or worked out and when we would leave. being in control felt great, I felt respected.

While grading someone else's essay, I've been in a position of power where I could choose to grade leniently or I could choose to grade harshly. When I was given the essay I recognized the person who wrote it as someone who I didn't care too much for. I decided to grade it more strictly and less laxly, because they hadn't committed actions that made me happy. They talked to me about the grade that I had given them, but I wouldn't give them a higher grade because I felt it was what they had deserved.

A time where someone else had power over me, was when I was at my internship where I had to give tours of the facilities. In this particular situation I could not express my ability to do more than I was asked to do. I felt incompetent because I knew that I could do more than simple task. My supervisor would give me the unimportant task to me to accomplish it.

My employer fired me without explaining themselves or the reasoning behind it. The lack of information made me feel powerless and confused. I also felt a bit upset while it was happening, but realized it was not worth my time if I was not given the opportunity to fix an error on my part.

It was when I found out that my transcripts were in hold. My transcripts needed to be send in order to transfer. It was close to the deadline and I remember I felt so frustrated because I couldn't contact anyone. I sent emails, called them and didn't get any response. I didn't have control in the situation since they were in charge of the situation. Finally, I got a response and my transcripts were send because I said I was going to talk to the president of the College if they didn't send my transcripts right away. :) It worked.

Last year I had to make the decision on where to attend college. I had little say to what college I would end up choosing. My parents had the last say in which school I went to due to the fact that money was tight. I would have to choose the college that offered me the most money. It was a situation that I understood, but was very sad I wouldn't really get to choose especially since my brother was already attending his dream school. I felt like I was in the shadow of my brother because of his choice to go to a University I would have to follow in those footsteps or even lower education because of the money problem.
I was in a position of power during work. I was able to control what students would do for me while at work. It felt good because I was able to give them the tasks that I did not want to do.

A few weeks ago, I was at my new job training for a position as a server. I had a trainer that I would listen to very intently and observe how she did certain tasks. She would then evaluate how I would conduct those same tasks and pay attention to the types of questions I asked. I felt somewhat intimidated because my trainer seemed to be an expert at serving and made it seem like it was her second-hand nature. However, after a few days of training I was getting the hang of it and managed to find my own rhythm.

I was both the lead photographer and editor-in-chief of my high school's yearbook. For the senior best section, I had several ideas that I thought would be great to portray one of the categories but they were all turned down by my advisor. He didn't believe it would "work". Normally, I think people would feel discouraged for being turned down so many times, but I was used to getting my ideas being shot down. The yearbook advisor isn't a perfectionist, but he would always find flaws in how I would portray my idea in the photo. He is concern more over the content, and through his critiques, I think I have a better idea of how I'd portray certain details in my photos. The standards are high and I didn't want people to say, "What happened this year?"

The first event that comes to mind took place during my senior year of high school. Mr. Beerman, his actual name, assigned a simple group project. I'm pretty sure I did the exact same project in elementary school. We were supposed to create a maze using quotes from the books we had read over the year. I had been a student of Beerman's previously, so it seemed artsy and straightforward, which we were used to at that point. I was gathered into a group and we made plans to complete the actual maze. Those plans fell through and we rescheduled due to cancellations from pretty much everyone. They had excuses, believable, so I changed the date and time. Then one group member flaked, the other ordered food and ate the entire night while the last member slept on my couch. I finished the project by myself the night before it was due. It looked like I finished it within the five minutes before it was due. I could have told Beerman they did not contribute, it would have been true and he would have believed me. But their grades hung in the balance, in Beerman's class it could have been the difference between an F and a D or a D and a C. I chose to allow them to have the points, to have the A that we probably didn't deserve. No reason, I guess.

When I applied for a job in high school I felt like I did not have power. Once you submit the application, it is up to the hiring manager if they want to hire you or not. I felt very anxious and vulnerable until I found out the I had the job.

Right now I am in a position of power on the volleyball team. I was appointed captain this year which is a big deal. I was really happy because I want to learn how to lead a team because I have never done that.

I honestly can't think of such a situation, sorry. I didn't want to just lie by making something up... I just really don't think I've ever been in a position of power like that, and If I have I can't recall.

During senior year of high school I was part of the people who chose the girls for the team for the following year. I got to evaluate the girls and pick if they were eligible to be a part of the team. I felt nervous because I knew some girls wouldn't make the cut even though they tried out and gave it their all. That was a bit sad, but at the same time I was excited and happy for the girls that would make it.

As I was growing up, I was in a position of power over my brother. He needed to ask for permission to have friends over or to go to a friends house as well as eating candy. I did not mind being in power, at times, because I am older than my brother therefore, I am the authority figure at the time. However, I did not like being in power if my brother had a tantrum because I would have to explain his behavior to our parents and be responsible for some of his actions at times.

When I played water polo against a really good team. The person guarding me did not allow me to score a goal because he played great defense and overpowered me in various occasions. I felt very frustrated because, no matter what I did, I could not score on him.
I honestly cannot remember.

As a member of my high school's Associated Student Body I was head of the Spirit Committee- which planned, organized, and executed school pep rallies, spirit weeks, and other events. I was in charge of ensuring the gym was set up and decorated properly and that everyone was on task and doing their part to contribute. I felt very productive and full of purpose, which made me content. I also liked helping people when they had questions or weren't sure of directions, so I got to help a lot in that way as head of Spirit Committee.
In my anthropology class, I was the group moderator, and I evaluated each person based on merit and participation. I evaluated each person in an unbiased manner.

I was trying to ask a person to go get dinner at this place, and when i said "must" go with me the person was somewhat not happy because i was forcing them. This is when i try to controlled the ability of another person, because i know the fact that the person has nothing to do other than staying home and relax. When i ask others to do something, they usually feel like i am demanding them.

My parents left for vacation and left me in charge of the house and my little siblings. I was looking after my siblings and was able to tell them what to do because if they did not do as I said I would have told my mom. At times we would fight and I would be mad with my siblings. I ended up not telling my parents everything because then we would all get in trouble.

When I was in junior high, I was a RA. The experience was fun because my job was walking around the dorm and told students to go to bed at night. If I heard them talking, I would warn them once. And if they were being loud again, I could give them a ticket. I loved my job because I interacted with different kinds of people during that time. I also tried to send a ticket to anyone buy calming the students that had trouble going to sleep. Even though my power was limited, I understood how difficult it was to avoid a fight.

I am a student-athlete so my coaches have power over how much playing time I receive. During one game my coach took me out before half-time without any explanation even though I felt I was playing well. I became frustrated and angry since I did not receive any input as to why I was taken out. After the game ended my coach took me aside and finally explained that he did not see as much effort as I usually put into the game. I said, "Okay I understand," even though I did not since my teammates agreed with me in that I was playing well. I did not argue back since he could have gotten angry at me, which could influence how much playing time I get in the next game.

A situation where someone had power over me occurred when I had been in my school's cafeteria and I had been sent to the back of the line because one of the lunch ladies hadn't liked how I had responded to her comments. I don't remember exactly what was said or done, but being sent to the back just because she was able to do that made me upset and helpless that no one would take me seriously and that I was essentially powerless to try and do anything otherwise.

I worked at Subway for almost a year, and dealing with the manager was very frustrating, since I was very dependent on the income, but had little say over the amount of hours I was given, or what I could do at work. I had requested working at least twenty hours a week upon being hired, but sometimes I would get as little as six hours on the schedule a week, due to conflicting schedules and worker seniority. This mad me very angry and frustrated at times, and also fueled the depression I was going through due to some other big life changes and choices I had been experiencing and making at the time. Dealing with my boss, who could be quite inept at times, on a daily basis was also a bit of a struggle for me, not to mention my coworkers...

A situation in which I recall this happened was in high school when I won the position for ASB Secretary.I remember one of the members really wanted this position, but at the end it really depended on who gave a very well/informative speech to the student body. I felt bad at first, but then again I knew the hard work i put into my speech had payed off at the end.

I had to grade someone's essay. I recognized the person who wrote the essay but didn't have any good feelings towards her. She ended up asking for a higher grade than what I had given her, but I decided to keep her grade the same way because I felt that I had given her a fair grade and was in no mood to help her.

In my research lab, the graduate student has power over me in regards to if I will be published or not in the next paper they are writing. She has the power to evaluate my contribution to the research and judge if that merits my name being in the publication. Because of this, I feel that I have to do a lot to prove myself and it is frustrating because I have no control over the situation.

An incident in which I was in a position of power was when I accompanied my grandmother to the urgent care along with my mother. My grandmother was consistently vomiting and claimed that she was experiencing chest pain. Between both my grandmother and my mom, I was the most fluent in English and therefore the only one able to communicate to the nurses about my grandmother's pain. The urgent care physicians informed us that they have an ambulance waiting to take my grandmother to the emergency room for fear that she was suffering a heart attack. My mom refused to believe that my grandma's condition was as terrible as the nurses described and suggested to my grandmother to simply go home and relax. At this point, it was my decision to tell the nurse whether my grandmother will take the ambulance or not. Because of my deep care for my grandma's health, I decided it was best to have my grandmother escorted to the hospital under close observation of the emergency medical technicians. As a result, my mom and I stayed with my grandmother at the hospital for over twelve hours but fortunately, was not diagnosed with anything serious. Had I not agreed to take my grandmother to the hospital, we would not have known that she was okay.

When at home, I don't feel as independent as when I am at school. My parents more closely monitor what I eat and do, as well as who I hang around. It makes me feel upset because I like to have a good time here at school but also like to be around my family.

I was at my job last year and had an incident where the customer had voiced her opinion while yelling. I, at the time, had gotten all read and had that pit in the back of my throat and was likely trying to speak which got the customer even more mad. Once I started to speak and try to ask what I could do to help she then proceeded to yell at me even more, for absolutely no reason. I felt powerless because I couldn't speak without her yelling and not to mention I was in a professional setting where I couldn't back talk the customer or I would get fired.

I am currently in the admissions class for the Honors Program at the University of Florida. I help score the essays that determine which students are accepted into the program and which are not. It is gratifying to be on the other side of the admissions process; only 6 months ago I was applying to the honors program myself. However, being in a position of power is more stressful when you can empathize with those who will ultimately get a rejection letter, especially when you are the one deciding that they do not make the cut. I enjoy being in the admissions class and scoring essays, I only hope the students who are not accepted learn from the failure rather than resenting the organization overall.

I was the captain of my club soccer team. I dictated our strategies and called out the plays during the game or at half time. The position made me feel empowered. I felt like i could say anything and my team would follow without a second thought.The position I held as the captain gave me more confidence. I felt like I could do anything.  I would like to be in such a position again as president of club or organization.
I was the captain of a hockey team in which the coach frequently asked me about others' playing time. I never told the coach to bench someone out of spite, only to help the team.

Recently, I had a friend open up to me about her problems with her family and her friends. After listening to her I felt like I knew her better. I tried to be very objective when listening to her but at the same time offered my sympathy when needed.

I was President of the Homecoming Committee my Senior year. I really liked the feeling of being in control of the other volunteers, because it meant that I could accomplish exactly what I wanted to for the project. I felt very much so in control.

I was chief of properties in my high school drama department. I had to divide tasks among multiple underclassmen to find, create and distribute different objects for the productions. I felt kind of stressed because it was my responsibility to make sure that everyone did what they needed when they needed and to fix any mistakes they made. It was also fun to be in a position of power and decide what aspects of the job I wanted to do and what I wanted to delegate.

A situation I did not have power in was earlier this Fall 2014 semester during Rush Week for fraternities. For an entire week you are constantly judged hoping and praying you'll get the bid you want. I personally felt powerless, I was acting like myself but felt like that wasn't adequate enough. In the end it all worked out but it felt like an eternity of waiting and multiple times where I felt worthless.

I was in a position of power during my group project last year in Warrington Welcome, which is an introduction business school class. I was in charge of a project where we had to create a fictitious business and create a business model for the company we created. I was in charge of delegating task and making sure that the project was correctly and efficiently. It was a decent amount of pressure but being in previous leadership positions helped me keep a level head and get the job done.
I guess when people are trying to get your vote to become president of an organization. You feel needed and important because they want something from you.

I did not have power when I had to complete standardized testing in elementary school through high school. I had to take the tests and needed to score well on them to move on to the next grade level or do go to a prestigious university. I felt like I was competing with my peers to do better than them to get into a better school than they did.

When I was a child I wanted to skateboard because all of my friends had one but my parents would not give one to me because they said it was not safe for me. And I couldn't do anything about it because I was too young to even earn some money to get one for myself. I was so mad at them because they would not give me one and I felt so helpless.
I was buying a ticket to the football game and the person I was buying it from had the power to sell it to me or to keep it. I felt anxious because I wanted to go to the game.

There was an anxiety and tension to display my ability submissively. In my speech class, this speech was the difference between the letter grade of an A or B. My speech teacher evaluating me made me very nervous and altered my natural abilities. While presenting I felt that my speech was not exceeding her expectations, let alone mine, because of the jitters and stuttering while presenting.
i was a gymnastic counselor and i enjoyed evaluating my students on their performance and help train them in there weaknesses to improve them for competition
Mom not letting me go out with friends when I was in middle school. I felt sad and angry because I did not understand why I could not be trusted to take care of myself.

When babysitting my younger siblings I am in charge of whether or not they receive rewards such as desert or television. When I am in charge they often try to take advantage of the fact that I am not the parent and will sometimes choose to ignore my authority; however, when they realize that I am in control of their rewards they will usually try to behave. It is sometimes frustrating to not be respected as an authority figure except when you are in control of what they want.

The most recent position in which I felt I did not have power was in a club meeting. The directors of the club did not listen to the suggestions of the other club members and decided what would happen without consulting the rest of us. I felt frustrated.

An incident when I was in power was when I was the Drum Major of my high school marching band. I was the man in charge in terms of making sure everyone was where they needed to be as well as controlling how the music was being played. It was stressful and demanding position because you are dealt with an extensive amount of responsibility but very rewarding in the end.

I played golf for my high school golf team and in my second year the coach decided to take another player to a tournament. At that tournament that player performed poorly and then the coach decided to take that same player to another tournament the next week over me again. Again that player performed poorly in the tournament. I felt that the coach decided who he wanted even if they were not playing better at the time of the tournament. It felt like he was playing favorites and I was the one that was left out. Later in the season I ended up winning one of the bigger tournaments that we played in and I got no recognition from the golf coach. It felt like he was trying to help some of his players to play better and had no confidence in other players which caused a lack of leadership on the team.

I recently went through recruitment. I was on the fence about going Greek but decided to try it anyways. I did not like the fact that I had no control over where I was invited back and where I was not. I thought I had great conversation at one house but then they would not invite me back. It sucked not knowing what would happen next.

I am a swim coach and one day the person who does the lowest group was sick and could not make it in and the person who has the group above mine was out so I covered three different age groups and maintained three different practices for each. My boss was doing another group with his assistant and they watched me critically during this practice. Before that day they have only seen me coach 5-10 children and in one group. Although this experience was highly stressful since each group were on completely different swim levels varying from beginners who could drown any minute to FLAG champs it was difficult to create a balance with all three groups so that everyone got a good workout and felt like the coach was coaching them and not just telling them what to do. At the end of it all I got a compliment from my boss saying "Good Job" which never happens and from his assistant saying that I was a good job and that he would not have been able to handle it himself.

I was interviewing for a job here at UF. It was a group interview and I felt intimidated because I knew everyone wanted the same thing and there was only one person in the room interviewing all of us at once. I felt like I had to stand out in order to get what I wanted.

As president of my high school's italian honor society, I was able to appoint others to specific positions and tasks, hear out their interviews and ask directed questions, and control all operations of the club. It felt good to be in a position of power in order to get things done efficiently

I was in charge of a small group of people that was set to revamp our high school whole library (Collecting books, making orders, working with the principal, laying out floor plans, etc.). The result was that the experience was partially consuming, but mostly rewarding and if its worth mentioning, this wasn't the first time I was ever in charge of something, but the most recent one. It felt great to be able to lead people and teach them what to do, for example, I would teach my assistants where to move boxes and how to scan books and later they would work alongside me. I must admit sometime I got lazy and worked less  than most of my assistants and it is frustrating to think that I could've done more, but in my defense, I was meant only to organize and teach people what to do. I remember a particular moment when we lost a huge collection of books (The dual enrollment books where placed in a different school since they are really valuable) for Dual Enrollment and my principal was fuming mad at the assistant who lost the collection. I took the blame and made sure that the assistant was let go of the charges. I had to pay for some of the books, but managed to find most of them afterwards with the help of my assistants at the time. I think that when it came to leading people it wasn't much of a problem or very complicated, it was more like being a teacher if anything.

The situation in which someone else had power over me was in high school when the Senior Army Instructor had the power to promote me to Battalion Commander or to keep me as the Battalion Executive Officer. Not only did he have the control over my ability to get something I wanted but was also in a position to evaluate me. In the end, I did not receive the promotion because he felt the position was better suited to a female due to the social aspect of the position during our upcoming inspection. I felt mad and disappointed at the fact that I had no power over the situation.
Being captain of my tennis team. I was able to make decision as to who would have the eligibility to play in a match and who would not
I don't think of having power, I simply believe in the delegation of tasks. Power can sometimes have a negative connotation.

When I was a new leader at my youth group, there was someone who was above me and would always negate my ideas and always had something to say about my leadership. I always felt like she was out to get me, no matter what the situation was. I felt helpless because she was my leader and it was her, if anyone, that I had to go to if I ever had a problem, but she was the problem.
When I wanted to attend this university, admissions officers had the power to accept me or not.

I was a counselor and had an assistant and he would basically have to do whatever i told him to. I felt powerful and thought that it was a great feeling. Honestly  I couldnt force him to really do much other than menial tasks like grab things for me or take attendance but it was still a great feeling.

When I used to work at Subway, one time this man came in angrily demanding for a new sub because it got "too soggy in the bag."  I could've decided not to make a new one for him because he had already payed for it, he was being very rude, and it wasn't my fault that happened, but I decided the customer should get what he wants.  I was annoyed by the way the man acted.  If he had just asked nicely I wouldn't have been so unwilling to make him a new sub.

I wrote a paper that I thought was really good and was approved by other students who proofread it for me, but the professor gave me a bad grade. After talking to the professor she refused to change the grade because it was decision.

My dad had power over me when I wanted to leave the house before doing my homework. I felt I would be able to do it when I got back so I was frustrated. I had to then finish the homework before I left.

When I was captain of cheerleading, I had the power to decide what our routines would consist of, what we would wear on game days, and where we would attend team dinners.  This experience made me feel very stressed.
Professors have some power over my grade. When they grade harshly on free response areas, it is an unpleasant experience.

When I volunteered at the Miami Children's Hospital, I worked in the lab and handled patient samples. Having the opportunity to use the centrifuge was very exciting. I would scan the samples to log them, then I would organize them according to their color. Most of the blood samples had to go in the centrifuge and I felt very powerful when I got to use it because I was in control of something new and exciting. I was controlling where each sample would go for further analysis and when they would be distributed. I saw many different types of patient samples that looked strange and interesting. Just being in control while working their was a little nerve wracking because I knew that people's lives would change depending on how the samples were processed and analyzed.
I was babysitting and the kids wanted to have ice cream but werent behaving so they didnt get any. I have no feelings about this.

I auditioned for the sedoctaves. They had the power over me to decide whether or not I could be in the group. They evaluated me and controlled my ability to get in. It made me feel apprehensive. I didn't get in, but I wasn't so upset because I knew that it was a rare chance that I would be let in.

I was captain of my soccer team and was able to have a say in the positioning of the team (who played where, the amount of players in each position). I love being in control. I feel confident and powerful when I know that my say matters.
In classes when teachers test you, you feel somewhat pressured under the power they have over you because they can grade, for example, an essay subjectively.

I was captain of my cheer leading team in high school, so I had power over those individuals. It's a struggle to establish yourself, as the "captain" after they have seen you for so long as another member of the team, or their "equal." I was determined to earn their respect, and I did. You just have to realize that sometimes you don't need to be their friend, but rather, someone who they can look up to, a leader.

I have been captain of my Hi Q team (trivia) so i could control who could join games or who had to leave.  To me it just felt like another task, something an adult assigned me to do and that I did just to comply with what I was told.

Applying to the University of Florida was a situation where power was completely one-sided. I worked hard and submitted my complete application to be reviewed. All I was able to do was wait. I had no say or voice in the decision on whether or not I would be accepted in the university. The school had all the power and was in complete control on whether I was accepted or not. This gave me such anxiety and the idea of attending or not attending the university never left my mind. I just kept thinking if the university doesn't accept me, how would I know why? They've never met me. They do not know everything I have accomplished or who I truly am. A piece of paper is what proved to them I was worthy on being accepted and that's completely absurd.

I did not have power over the amount of financial aid money I received when applying for college. Of course some receive more than others but this caused me to chose a school over the cost rather than my first choice.

Working for my family in the brewery that my brother owns. Since it is my family, I was not on the payroll and so did a great deal of manual labor for very little money if at all. It was exhausting and didn't feel worth it, even though I was helping my family.

My senior year in high school I was Senior Coordinator for my health program and I was in charge of approving applications for an internship at the University of Miami Hospital. If people were rude to me, if I felt they weren't competent enough, or if I knew they would simply embarrass our school at the hospital, I declined their application. I didn't feel sorry for anyone.

I was in Gator Corner Dining Hall and they were serving sliced turkey on a bun with potatoes, green beans or peas, and cranberry sauce. When I asked for just turkey (without all the extras), the lady behind the counter gave me an aggravated look and said that I can only have the turkey with all of the side dishes, which I did not want. I did not understand why it was so hard for her to just pick up a single piece of plain turkey and put it on my plate. I was extremely aggravated and frustrated that I could not have what I wanted for lunch, so I walked away to another station.
I always feel powerless when I am confined to a room and not supposed to leave unless I ask for permission, so like when taking the SAT or ACT. It makes me feel anxious.

My dad and I recently had a conversation about my monthly allowance. He told me that it would be x amount of dollars and that was the end of it. He did not allow me to have a say in the situation and said this is how it's going to be. I felt it was unfair. People should always have the chance to voice their feelings and opinions no matter the circumstances before a decision is made.

In high school, I had the choice to take IB Math Studies or IB Mathematics. I wanted to choose Math Studies because it was easier and would get me an easy A. My parents wanted me to take Mathematics instead and forced me into it, knowing that my background in math was not the best. I felt angry, annoyed, and resentful over the decision. I kept complaining throughout the year that it was too hard and I struggled to get an A, but my parents would keep saying that I wasn't trying my best and would scold me when I got a bad grade. I kept seeing how easy it was for the other students and the free time they had instead of studying so hard like I did. I felt jealous and robbed of an opportunity that I wanted, but what my parents took from me.

It felt good to know that other people looked up to me and sought answers. They looked at me as if I had some greater power over them. They asked me questions and wanted my approval. It's nice to be in a position of authority.

The other day I had to go pick someone up to go shopping because they didn't have a car. If I hadn't had a car, I don't know how we would have gone shopping. I was frustrated by the fact that he didn't have a car, but I was also pleased and grateful that I did. It reminded me fondly of my freshmen year of college when I drove almost all my friends around because I was one of the only ones with a car.

I was in charge of a fashion team. I decided what each model was wearing, what fabric I needed to make the designs, and the coordination of the fashion team. It was stressful, exciting, and fun to be in charge.

Trying out for high school cheerleading. The judges determined whether your skills were good enough to put you on a team. They had the power to decide if you were good enough, even if you had confidence that you were. It makes you try your best, but at the same time makes you resent them if they don't give you what you wanted even if you tried your best.

I was performing a basic evaluation at the gym to determine my levels of fitness and to develop an exercise plan. I felt the instructor's constant hovering in order to evaluate my skills made me uncomfortable. I also did not like being told to continue the exercise, for I would have much preferred a set of repetitions to complete as opposed to it being subjective. This made me feel like I was not doing well because I needed to repeat the exercise. I would have much preferred to self-report the data.

The situation in mind (out of many) was the many months of waiting for an admission decision from the University of Florida. Having gone through community college for two years, I worked very hard to have the best shot at transferring to the University of Florida. Not only was I excited that I felt like a great applicant (because of my gpa), but I was eager to leave the gloomy atmosphere that I endured for two long years. Awaiting for the decision I felt very anxious. I had looked forward to University of Florida for two years, and all other universities in Florida would have been a continuation (or close to it) to my community college experience. Needless to say, several weeks preceding my acceptance were arguably some of the worst times in my life. The acceptance made all the difference in the world, and will never forget that day.

Being the President of Senior Class Council, it felt at times great to be in power instead of doing the labor work but yet again very stressful because people were waiting for your every command. There was also high expectations to whether you would get the task done right.

Student org chair interview. I felt like I was determining there fate because I was one of the people that would decide whether or not they would get the position that they applied for. I felt powerful and above them.

In a leadership retreat, instruction on how to build a dinosaur was given. We were supposed to assemble it and then explain the instructions quickly to a group outside of the room which had never seen the dinosaur. When the group came in, there was some confused looks towards what they were going to do, and a lot of noise. I stood up in a chair and loudly told the groups to separate in two teams, one would do the lower body and the other would do the upper body of the dinosaur. I felt accomplished because the result was that they assembled the dinosaur faster than we did and without looking at instructions or pictures.
I was bullied in Fifth grade because the students were jealous of my good grades. They asserted power over me in order to make me feel less than what I am.

I was a camp counselor this past summer. I was in charge of ten 6-9 year olds for three months. I basically had to be their mother for that time. I had to be in control and tell them to clean up and be nice to each other. I didn't really enjoy constantly having to tell them what to do.

I was the student body treasurer of my high school and had the responsibility of interviewing those students who wanted to hold their class treasurer position. I was required to read their applications and interview those who I thought were the best fit for the job. I felt very in control of the situation and did my best not to abuse the power by making sure my decision was unbiased.

I remembered being judged at an All State Competition for Band and I had no control on how the judge would respond to me. Yes, I had worked hard and practiced but sometimes even the smallest misuse of technique is enough to tick off a judge. I remember feeling scared and uncertain because I had very little control over what the judge thought and if in fact he thought I was a good player or an average player.

I was president of the Nation Honor Society at my high school. When the time came to introduce new members, i knew which ones were chosen and which ones became ineligible. Also, when officer positions became open, i had to vote for the ones i wanted to be in office. I felt really responsible for the whole situation and all of the outcomes. It was hard to take such a big responsibility on especially if i knew the people that were becoming members. I felt sort of bad most of the time because i didnt know if i made the right decisions.

I was forced to attend a family friend's party which I did not want to go to. I would have much rather wanted to stay home or go somewhere else. But my parents said I had to go with them. It was boring, I didn't want to be there, and I wanted to go home. I was in a bad mood, or not pleasant as I usually am and it was noticeable in my appearance.

I was being interviewed by a group of three adults from an organization in order to be selected for a scholarship. I felt extremely nervous, especially when I noticed that I was the sole focus of their attention. They were the determiners of whether or not I would receive a scholarship, and so I chose every word carefully and cringed at my mistakes in answering their questions.
I was Editor in Chief of my high school newspaper. I felt stressed and anxious, but slightly relieved that I got to control the process.

The last time I was in power where it affected the ability and wants of a person was last year. I was President of a club, and my director asked me to choose someone to speak to a group of students. Instead of choosing my Vice President, I instead chose another person whom my director and myself has given the title of Ambassador. U made this decision, because the Ambassador was outgoing and relatable, while my Vice President was somewhat dull. The VP only ran for the position because she thought that herself and our friend and the time would be President and Vice President together. I did not make the decision to not invite her, but to choose who qualified the most and who would bring more member to the club. I felt okay with this decision, and I wouldn't change it. I made a decision that bettered the club, not the decision that better suited the VP.

I was captain of the color guard team at my high school. Every practice the instructor would tell me what we had to get done. I felt like it was very difficult to gain the respect of other students who knew me before I was captain while the other students who I met as captain respected me and followed instructions. It was very frustrating getting lectures when the team did not finish everything on time but I felt like I had no control over them.

I was applying for a job at a retail store called Delias. It was the only store that called me back for an interview. Before going to the interview I practiced speaking in front of a mirror and thought of possible questions my manager would ask me. I was nervous but excited at the same time. I was a little stressed. I was 16 and felt that I needed to get a job as soon as possible because my older brothers also had jobs when they were old enough to. I tried to make my self seem as marketable as possible, and told my manager that I loved Delias and shopped there all the time.
Whenever I want something from a store, but my parents say I can't have it. I felt angry.
This past summer I worked at the YMCA summer camp as a camp counselor. I had a position of power over the campers, and I felt like I was respected as an adult.

In high school I was vice president of the senior class. I had the power to help make decisions regarding what we spent our money on, t-shirt designs, class song, flower, etc. Having this type of power was some what stressful because if something went wrong I was going to take a big part of the blame. I always had to think what was going to be best for everyone not just myself.

I was in charge of putting together a dodge ball tournament and the person under me was a boy.  He thought because it was a boy's sport that he could run it more efficiently than me.  I ran it the first year and it went off without a hitch he ran it the second year and everything was a disaster and I had to fix everything while he got all the credit.  I feel as if girls can do anything boys can do, sometimes even better.  He felt it was his right to run this male based event but when he was actually in charged failed and then relied on me to do everything, while taking the credit.

In high school I was founder and editor in chief of the online newspaper. This position gave me a lot of power because I was in control of the assignments the students had to complete, the curriculum of the class, their grades, etc. I don't really remember feeling a particular way for being in power, I just remember feeling like I wanted to bring the staff together to provide other students with credible and timely information. In the beginning of the school year it was a little difficult for the other students to take me seriously because I was a similar age as they were, but once they realized that I wasn't in my position for power, but rather was in it to bring everyone together to provide for others, they began respecting me.

When I was in a situation where I did not have power, I was in class in 12th grade. I needed to deliver a check for a club I was in, and that time frame conflicted with field hockey practice. My coach would not let me leave early, so I did not get to deliver the check on time, which caused a problem with the orders for the club. I was upset, since there was nothing I could do about it, but I felt like I let everyone in the club down.

High school comes to mind, as at the time I felt I had limited freedom. You had to ask a teacher just to use the restroom and your lunch hour, your movements, and your attendance were dictated by bells and schedules. Overall, this made me feel like a child and trapped, in a sense.

My manager at an old job had power over whether or not I would receive a particular promotion. My manager evaluated and made her decisions about employees based on how she liked them personally, not on their ability to complete work or their efficiency. Another co-worker of mine ended up getting the promotion instead of me, due to the fact that she had known the manager for longer than I had. This made me feel very upset because the power over my job was in the hands of someone who was biased.

I was out with some friends one night for a movie premiere, but the movie ended late. My parents knew where I was because I asked them for permission to go out beforehand, but they still punished me for coming home later than expected, even though I had nothing to do with it. I wanted to talk back and contradict what they were saying, but I decided against it because I knew that I would get into even more trouble over something that already seemed so stupid and pointless. I felt like I had no say and like my parents couldn't trust me, even though I never do anything bad or rebellious, like so many other kids do. I study hard and have my priorities set straight, but even so, my parents put me on a tight leash and it can get very annoying very quickly.

In the summer I had a job as a valet. There was a small group of us an we took turns being in charge of the keys and the incoming cars. when it was my turn there was a rush of cars so i had to tell everyone which car to get in and tag them so we could handle it all. it was very interesting, I was able to stay calm even when everyone was parking cars. I was happy with myself when we finished because everything went smoothly.

When I was in high school, my teacher gave us a lot of homeworks and he said we have to finish all of those homeworks in 3 days. Although we said that is unfair, he just forced us to finish all of homeworks. At that time, I felt so embarrassed and confused because I couldn't understand why I should finish those homeworks in 3 days.

As a director of a program under a large student organization, the president and many other departments such as the registrar and SG office, have a lot of power over what I do within my own program. Sometimes, it frustrates me whenever I can't get something approved or done because those of a higher power do not understand the importance or urgency of a certain task I need them to do. But, I do try to understand that they have a lot of other organizations/programs to deal with so I try not to be annoying and just submit my favors early in order to give them time.

During sorority recruitment each chapter evaluated us and had control to drop us from their recruitment. It was hard to deal with and it made me a little anxious to know that they controlled which house I could get into.

One position where someone had power over me was when I auditioned for my high school band's squad leader position. I felt very nervous as I performed my piece of music and gave the interview. In the end I was selected as one of the squad leaders. That felt very satisfying.

I was in a position of power in last weekend when I was responsible for giving my friends a ride home. I had to take 4 of them back to Orlando and so 2 of them were being very nice to me because they knew that at any second I could tell them that they could not ride back with me. I felt as though it was only right that I gave them a ride back home because I would want them to do the same for me. They said they were extremely thankful that i gave it to them and so they gave me gas money because they would have spent it riding the bus anyway.

When applying to college or for anything, the institution had the power to evaluate me and decide a very large part of my future, whether or not I would be accepted or given the opportunity to join them. It's in my power to present my best case, but the power is all theirs in wanting me. I couldn't control their decision, but I could mine and when I got rejected it only made me want to be a better than I was to prove them wrong. There is more than one way of getting the same thing done and once something fails, I just want to find another way to overcome this "greater" power.

I worked at a retail clothing store over the summer and my manager would control everything I did. When I took breaks, when I clocked in and out, when I left, what I would do that day, etc. Many times my manager would make me take a break almost an hour earlier than I was scheduled to, which annoyed me. I didn't mind having someone in power over me at this job, I did not like it when they asserted their power.

A position in which someone else had power over me were my parent's control over my curfew and where I could and could not go in high school. Curfews made me feel very limited in what I could and could not do. I am the type of person that likes to be in control of my own decisions, and not have someone hovering over what I can and cannot do. If I was late, I knew I would be punished, and if I was home early I knew I would miss something important or fun that my friends would be doing. Punishments instilled fear into me and missing out on fun things or exciting events made me feel lonely or like I was letting someone down. Both of these situations cause me great levels of anxiety because I do not like to disappoint others.

I was in a program called JROTC. I desired to be the battalion commander and the people in power of my desire becoming reality or not were my instructors and peers. I felt motivated to succeed and in the end I did.

As the vice president of a county-wide organization two years ago, I felt pressure and responsibility to get many plans and events into action. It was a good feeling to complete tasks but the pressure from others within the organization was substantial.

Being a coach of a high school cross country team that I attended. I would organize practice, meetings, races etc. The athletes felt very confident with me as there coach and knew that I knew what I was doing and they trusted me. I felt our team relationship as a whole was very good and we had great team commrodary which in turn ended up with a state championship in Track.
An interview to get a scholarship. I got interviewed. I was nervous and my legs were shaking.
My boss at work. She had control over my lifeguard testing and certification. I felt nervous and cautious of what I was doing.
I can not recall any experiences in which someone else had power over me.

I wanted to come up with my own class schedule for fall, but I was told that my plan wouldn't work out by my adviser. Therefore, I couldn't take one of the classes that required his permission. I was mad that there is no way for me to discourage his decision in order to accomplish my goal.
Coaching a pop warner team of children between the ages of 12 and 15 I frequently experienced being in a position of power. I felt the same amount of responsibility for every success and failure.

A situation in which someone else had power over me was when I wanted a new iPhone that had been recently released and I could not get the phone unless I followed my mother's rule of buying an otterbox case for the cell phone and if I did not buy the case, I wasn't allowed to buy the phone. I felt upset because I was buying the phone with my own money but wasn't allowed to buy it unless I followed my mother's stipulations upon purchasing the phone.

I was a drum major in high school. I had to evaluate section leaders performance. I didn't want to give anyone a bad report even if they did something wrong, but it was necessary in order for them to get better.
I did not have power in choosing if I was hired at my current job or not. I felt like there was nothing I can do. I felt helpless and useless like I just was stuck waiting.

I worked for three summers as a camp counselor. One day, my five year old camper demanded extra snack and threatened to call her mother if I didn't comply. Since I was the one in charge, I took away her phone and denied her request. I also made her have a time-out for being so rude. I enjoyed that I was able to tell someone else what to do and stop bad behavior. Being in a position of power makes me feel more confident.

When I was in high school, my mother had power over me at times. One time, when I wanted to go to a party, she refused to let me go because I had not cut the grass that week. In order to prevent me from going to the party, she took my car keys and hid them, so I was unable to go. I know that my mom was trying to teach me to do my chores around the house, but the feeling of being powerless and not being allowed to do as I wished, felt horrible. I felt trapped in my house and I became angry and irritable.

My coach had the power to put me on the field. Although I wanted a position on the field I did not have the power to choose it. I feel left out and discouraged when she has this power over me because there is nothing i can do about it.

The last situation was when I was being interviewed for an internship position at Nielsen. I was interviewed by two men who worked for the company, specifically in the program I had applied for, and they asked me several behavioral and technical questions. Throughout the interview I responded well and felt relatively calm the whole time - however, I was still "walking on eggshells" internally, carefully choosing what words, examples, and phrases I'd use to answer the questions.

When I was younger, I was the captain on my cheer leading team and I was able to choose different events that I wanted to participate in and had the opportunity to choose 5 people I wanted to work with. Nobody else couldn't choose and I was the only person with that opportunity.

In my online math class if I accidentally input the wrong letter variable or am off by a variable small amount the computer automatically marks the answer wrong. It is very frustrating sometimes because if a real teacher was grading my work they probably wouldn't mark something so small incorrect. I felt helpless and annoyed at the power the automatic grading had over me.

I was the captain of a Relay for Life team for two years in my hometown. I had to organize fundraisers and events that would allow our team to participate in the Relay for Life event that is held once a year. I loved being a team captain because I felt much closer to the event and I liked feeling that I was in control of what was going on with my team, and I knew that I could make sure that we got everything done that needed to get done. If people wanted to be a part of the team and get the community service hours that they wanted, they had to participate in a way that I felt was honorable by the American Cancer Society and in a way that made our team look good.

In high school I auditioned for a prestigious dance group and did not make it in my junior year. I felt cheated and upset that the teacher deciding had so much power, and I felt that I deserved to be in the group. I was angry and upset, but I auditioned for my senior year and made it into the group. However, I still feel resentment towards this woman.

In high school, I stepped up to run French club because no one else would do it and meetings and events were not be run properly. I planned meetings, times, activities, projects, etc. I felt relieved because it felt like me and everyone else actually enjoyed the club and we were finally doing exciting things. I was also stressed because if something didn't go right, people would blame me and people often came to me with their problems.

When working on a group project for physics, I took the lead and directed everyone to get it done. It was stressful and annoying; the group members would not focus and kept messing around while I was trying to work.

My coaches have power over me everyday. From the second we enter practice or workouts, we are being evaluated by our performance and how well we can complete a physical task. Since I do have a good relationship with my coaches, I'm more relaxed than others. But at times I do feel stressed to perform at my best and in hectic situations because they expect so much out of you at all times. Also, the fact that they are evaluating your skill level and not you as a person. This is an everyday thing, but I feel like the situation never gets easier since you are always being judged.

Well, I made a new friend when I first came to UF. Since I wanted to be friendly to him, I followed and took actions what he liked to do. For example; since he wanted to play tennis, I played tennis with him even though I am not good at playing tennis, and I need to write a paper for class. So I didn't feel like to play tennis. But I did in order to be friendly to him. I feel bad about the situation that I couldn't have power over the situation since he was my first friend in my new university life.

I used to be a Sunday school teacher and I was in charge of a class of 5th graders. I felt important because I was the one making all of the decisions and I was instilling the information in them. It made me feel good that if they had a question or needed something they came to me about, and I was the one with the final say and approval.

A few weeks ago I was selling my UF football ticket and was discussing my price with the buyer. The buyer realized I would not change my price and decided to pay me the price I was asking for the ticket. In this situation I had control over the buyers ability to get something they wanted. Being in control of the situation allowed me to sell the ticket for the price I wanted, because I had something the buyer wanted. Being in control allows me to be more comfortable and confident.

In my audition for the school's colorguard, I was the only one auditioning because I had missed the earlier audition date. It was very awkward first of all because the coach was basically comparing me to the girls who already has more practice with the choreography than I did. I was sectioned off from the rest of the girl who had already made it, but still in their view during my audition. I felt pressured to do very well in my audition because I thought the coach would be expecting a lot from me. She was going to give the final say on whether I could continue practicing with the group. It was nerve-wracking knowing that if I did not perform well them she would send me home on the spot in front of all the girls. I tried to avoid thinking about it, though.

When I lived at home, my parents had the power to let me or not let me attend football games. When they wouldn't let me go, I was upset and angry. I couldn't comprehend their reasoning. I never rebelled and always let go of my anger quickly.

When I had a part time job in high school, I wanted to get a raise after working there for 6 months. I was to go through a thorough evaluation process in order to get a raise. When I was going through the evaluation and after when my boss confronted me on how I did, I felt anxious. Feeling like I did my best and deserved a raise but not having control over whether or not I got it was not a position I enjoy being in. It made me feel weak.

The situation involved a grade dispute between myself and a teacher. At first, I felt that I was completely right and would do anything to prove it. Eventually, I lost hope and gave in (to the grade the I felt was incorrect).

I was captain of my high school's softball team my senior year. I instructed them during practices and games. I felt good that people were listening to me and following my instructions because it made me feel like I had gained their respect. Although I enjoyed the power that I had over my team, I was never power hungry and never treated anyone with disrespect.

When I was interviewed by a representative from MIT, the woman interviewing me had the power to evaluate me and influence my admission. I felt fine. I felt confident because I felt as though she would think highly of me.

I was team captain of my high school's volleyball team. I had a lot of input on who got to play in the games and how the practice was ran. I always tried to make sure everyone could play, but still made sure the team was able to win as many games as possible. It was stressful at times because not everyone was always satisfied and they would always complain to me.

During high school applications in eighth grade, I tried applying to one of the high schools that had the IB program. I really wanted to get into the program because I heard that one of my friends got into the program - a person who I felt didn't deserve to be in such an elite program since she was always going out every night and never did her homework. However, when I talked to my guidance counselor before I submitted my online application to the school board, she told me that I would not be accepted into the IB program because I didn't have the foreign language requirement. I was shocked and hurt. I was one of the top students in my class, but since I decided that I didn't want to take Spanish in middle school, I've been rejected before I even sent in my application. Since I could only choose one magnet program in the application, I was forced to give up my hopes of getting into the IB program and settled for a different magnet program.

When i was back in high school i was a captain on my football and track team so i could get freshman and sophomores to do what i want because they have to listen to me. I felt like i was the king and they were my servants i didn't have to do anything i didn't want to do. They thought it was mean but everyone have to go through it in high school unless you become a captain your freshman year like me.

In high school I was Co band captain and Section Leader. I ran my section and I taught them how to be good musicians, I also would press the fact that school came first and without school they wouldn't be in the band. One of my freshman had received a couple of F's on his report card and as the section leader that made me look like a terrible leader. I sat down and talked to him to figure out why his report was terrible. He was a class clown and therefore I punished him and he couldn't participate in any band events.  It was sad for me to but I had to teach him a lesson and me doing that he improved his grades. I used my power for good, because he improved on his school work.

As a members of the board it was my duty to assess potential new recruits by interviewing them. I would conduct the interviews in a casual setting so that the interviewee would feel at ease, however I made sure to be completely serious about the questions, taking notes and scoring their answers on a rubric. I made sure my language and conversation pertained to the matters at hand and I corrected the interviewee at the end of the interview, pointing out the flaws in his or her answers. I felt like a teacher and guide to the interviewees.

When we were playing soccer our junior year we had a new coach for one game and he did not know who played what and how much. I felt powerless because he did not play me even though i was a usual starter. I felt horrible and that I was not in control of anything.

I am a treasurer for the BSW club here at Southern Miss. As treasurer I balance our club's finance and am in control of writing checks to other members if needed for certain projects or functions. I like having this control because I know i'm very fixated on ensuring that our club stays on budget while also helping.

The only situation I can remember that is vaguely like that was when I was in elementary school, and someone gave me an IQ test to see if I could be put in the Gifted program.  I was very nervous, and unsure if I was completing the tasks correctly.

I guess I would recall the incident of when I wanted new softball bats but the coach would not buy them. I felt left down that he would not buy them and that I would be a bother to my parents if I asked them.

On my job my boss followed me around for a day. She was evaluating my performance so she could determine if I would receive a raise and how much. I felt very nervous I didn't know if I was doing things to her standard in order to receive the raise. If I did them correctly would it be enough to receive the highest raise you could get. The pressure was really on.

An employer. I was a single mother with no car and had to walk to work. I needed to provide for my children as well as three other siblings. I worked two jobs and tried my best to juggle them. Usually, I had four hours of sleep a night and had a rare day where I was not suppose to work. One of my employers made me feel that I had to come in to cover another person's shift or I would lose my job. Although I was exhausted and looking forward to spending time with my family, I went to work. I needed the job and had few options or so it seemed at the time. I was upset as well to feel I was put in that situation.

Well, there was this time where I wanted clarity. I was sick of getting unclear answers. I hated that feeling. Definite answers are what I operate on. They are what the world operates on.. I felt completely aloof and powerless. I cannot stand that feeling and wish to never feel it. But, alas, it happens more often than I'd wish.

When I was a small child, I would often be locked out of my cousin's room for whatever reason. Sense I was only about 6 years old at the time, I had no real problem-solving skills to get into the room and did not want to bully my way in via adults. It was definitely depressing to not be part of this "exclusive" group that was allowed into my cousin's room and be left out in the hallway for no real reason.

Being put in a situation of power is a stressful one. Telling someone what to do or that they can or cannot have something they desire is stressful. Evaluating individuals based on the way they are presented is also difficult. Telling someone what to do is an easy task. Delegating someone to perform a certain task is simple and does not take any certain amount of fear or uncertainty.

I was once in charge of a classroom filled with 5th graders. I had to teach them their lesson for that day and make sure they were behaving as if their teacher was in the room. I was only in one grade higher than so I felt afraid to teach them. I was thinking that they wouldn't respect me being that I wasn't much older than some of them.

One occasion that I had power in was the time I was placed in charge for a few hours while my manager ran to another store to deliver supplies. I had somewhat of authority and was able to get the employees to do what is asked of me. As being in charge, I was able to see how a person did each task. I could examine if the job was done properly and efficiently. I liked being in charge, but it was only temporary.

When I was in my last relationship I felt like i had no control over my partner as she berated me. She told me I was no good and that I was barely a person or anyone. I felt small and devalued like I was a no one. It mad me realize that I didn't have to take it so I left.

My friend needed a place to stay and at the time I did not have a lot of money for my bills.So because I had power over her, I made her pay most of the bills that I did not have money for or she would have to move out. For awhile I felt bad because I was using her but after I examined the situation I felt it was fair because she could not stay anywhere else for free.

I work in retail as a manager. We are told to follow the coupon procedure of one coupon per transaction. We as also told to make the customer happy, basically no matter what. Sometimes customers come into the store and try to use more than one coupon. Usually the customer is ok whenever I tell them they can only use one coupon per transaction. Other times they get upset and say that if they can use all of their coupons then they don't want to purchase anything at all. So by company standards of making the customer happy, I let the customer combine coupons. I hate when this happens because we are told one thing by the company and then have to go against it to follow another procedure the company wants us to uphold.

One time back in high school i was in charge of the entire woodwind section in my high school marching band. Being the only senior that day that was responsible enough I had to take charge and keep all the underclassmen in my section under control and on task. I did not like the feeling of being in charge of them very much because I thought that if I slacked up at all that day the would go wild and lose focus.

An incident that I can think of in which I was in a position of power is when my husband let me choose what we were eating for dinner. My thoughts were that I wished that he would make the decision. I would give him an idea of what I wanted or didn't want and tell him to choose from there. In another words, I would give my power back over to him.
When I tried out for the Southern Misses Dance team the coach had power over me because I knew I had to do what she wanted to make the team.

I have run into several problems with power when it comes to English Professors. I would make a certain argument in a paper, but because the argument was not necessarily in conjunction with the professor's beliefs they would subtract points. They would stand firm in their view of my paper and not give me any points back even when I explained the various arguments and their validity.
i felt like i had the disadvantage. i felt like the weak one and i was upset.

In high school I was in office of many organizations. For National Honor Society I was the president. At my school, we did our "Honor Roll Programs" on stage. I conducted the whole thing, I decided who would sit on stage and who wouldn't. I also determined who would make a speech or call out names during the program. I felt very honored to be the president, I was organized and was always ready. I hated being the determining factor of who sat on stage sometimes because I did not want my friends to get upset if I felt like their grades was not high enough for the honor.

I wanted to attend Southern,but i was staying in Meridian MS. I was working at JCPenneys at the time and i wanted to transfer from Meridian's store to hattiesburgs store. We had just received a new manager who  was not very friendly, which made our first impression terrible. I went to her and asked if she could transfer me and she told me no, and that she would not need my services at JCPenneys anymore. She basically fired me over the phone after i had been employed there for four years. That situation really made me upset and discouraged for future employments
When the teacher make the test really hard.

When I auditioned for a music ensemble here at school, my professor had the power of me top place me where she felt I belonged, based on my abilities. I felt nervous because I did not know how she would react or grade my audition.
